contribute:0.en: The Manager called us all to the back room before the weekend sale. 'Everyone must *contribute* something,' he said, spreading his arms wide. Tang brought homemade cookies for the display table. I straightened every shelf label twice. Even the old mop in the corner got a new head. The store had never looked so ready.
contribute:0.cnHint: 店长要求每个人都为周末大促____一份力，连拖把都换了新头。
contribute:0.hook: Then the Manager pulled out a karaoke machine and smiled.
contribute:0.line: 'Each of us must *contribute* something to make this sale work.'

share:0.en: Tang divided the weekend tasks into three lists and gave each of us a *share* of the work. My list had thirty items. Hers had thirty-one. She noticed my look and laughed, crossing one off hers and adding it to mine. 'Fair is fair,' she said. I wondered if she was always this careful about fairness.
share:0.cnHint: 阿糖把工作分成三份，把自己的一个任务划到我____里，说"公平就是公平"。
share:0.hook: But item thirty-one on my list just read: 'ask Tang.'
share:0.line: 'Here, take this task — your *share* should be equal to mine.'

decade:0.en: A quiet man came in at midnight and stood before the instant noodle shelf for a long time. 'I have eaten this brand every Friday for a *decade*,' he said softly, picking up a cup. He paid without another word and walked back out into the dark street. Ten years of Friday noodles. I found that both sad and oddly comforting.
decade:0.cnHint: 一位男顾客说他吃这款泡面已经整整____了，每周五都来买一杯。
decade:0.hook: The receipt in the drawer showed his first visit was exactly ten years ago today.
decade:0.line: 'I have bought this same noodle every Friday for a *decade*.'

kind:0.en: The Manager told me the weekend crowd would bring every *kind* of customer: the bargain hunter, the lost tourist, the sleepy student, the one who just needs somewhere warm to stand. 'Be ready for all of them,' he said. By two in the morning I had met at least four new types he had forgotten to mention.
kind:0.cnHint: 店长说周末会来各____各样的顾客，让我做好准备。
kind:0.hook: The fifth type walked in carrying a live fish in a plastic bag.
kind:0.line: 'This weekend you will see every *kind* of person walk through that door.'

across:0.en: Lin appeared at the window of the store *across* the street and stared at our sale banner for a full minute. Then they taped up their own banner. Then a bigger one. Tang watched quietly beside me and said, 'This happens every season.' The two banners faced each other all night like two dogs refusing to blink.
across:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在街____的店里挂起了比我们更大的促销横幅，阿糖说这每季都会发生。
across:0.hook: By morning, Lin had added a third banner and a small fog machine.
across:0.line: 'Look — Lin just put a new sign up *across* the street from ours.'

factor:0.en: Tang was calculating the final price tags and muttered that shelf position was the biggest *factor* in what people actually bought. She moved the most profitable item from the low shelf to eye level without asking anyone. Sales on that item tripled before midnight. The Manager never noticed, or pretended not to.
factor:0.cnHint: 阿糖说货架位置是影响销量的最大____，她悄悄把商品移到视线高度后销量翻了三倍。
factor:0.hook: Then she told me she had a degree in something I did not expect.
factor:0.line: 'Shelf height is the biggest *factor* — it decides what people pick up.'

condition:0.en: An older woman came in and examined every peach with great care before choosing one. 'Young man, the *condition* of the fruit tells you everything about the store,' she said. She was right — two peaches in the back were soft. I moved them to the front of my mind and the back of the shelf. She smiled and bought three.
condition:0.cnHint: 一位老太太说水果的____能说明一家店的一切，然后精挑细选了三个桃子。
condition:0.hook: She left a small handwritten note inside the basket that I only found the next morning.
condition:0.line: 'The *condition* of your fruit tells a customer everything they need to know.'

effort:0.en: At the end of the long Saturday night, Tang handed me a small cup of warm tea. 'Good *effort* tonight,' she said simply. Every shelf was straight, every label faced forward, the floor was clean. I was tired in a way that felt earned. Outside, the street was quiet and the sky was just beginning to go pale.
effort:0.cnHint: 阿糖递给我一杯热茶，说我今晚____得不错，我感到一种踏实的疲惫。
effort:0.hook: Then she said, 'Same time Sunday — but Lin will probably show up in person.'
effort:0.line: 'Good *effort* tonight — the store has never looked this clean.'

compare:0.en: The Manager had taped two price signs side by side on the snack shelf. 'Customers always *compare* before they buy,' she said, straightening them with care. I watched a student pick up both bags of chips, hold them at eye level for a long moment, and then — to my great surprise — put them both in his basket.
compare:0.cnHint: 店长把两个价格牌并排贴好，说顾客买东西前总会____一番。
compare:0.hook: He grabbed a third bag from the back row without even looking.
compare:0.line: 'Customers always *compare* before they buy — so make the signs easy to read.'

past:0.en: Tang leaned on the counter during a quiet hour and said the store used to close at midnight. 'That's all in the *past* now,' she sighed, nodding at the neon sign outside that read OPEN 24 HRS. I asked what changed. She smiled, poured herself a cup of hot water, and said simply, 'The neighbourhood grew up.'
past:0.cnHint: 唐靠在柜台上说，店里通宵营业只是近年的事，那些早早打烊的日子都已是____了。
past:0.hook: She never did explain what she meant by 'grew up.'
past:0.line: 'That's all in the *past* — we stay open through the night now.'

suffer:0.en: A regular came in just after two in the morning, rubbing his eyes and muttering. He had been studying for six hours straight and said his back had begun to *suffer* from sitting so long. I handed him a small heat patch from the shelf near the register. He stared at it like I had read his mind, then quietly paid and shuffled back into the dark.
suffer:0.cnHint: 一位常客深夜进店，说久坐让他的背开始____，我递给他一贴暖贴。
suffer:0.hook: He was back the next night at the exact same hour.
suffer:0.line: 'My back starts to *suffer* after five hours at the desk — it never fails.'

almost:0.en: I *almost* knocked over an entire display of instant noodles while reaching for a box on the top shelf. The tower swayed, every cup wobbling in a slow, terrible wave. I held my breath. One cup tipped — and stopped. Tang watched the whole thing from the door to the back room and slowly began to clap.
almost:0.cnHint: 我伸手够高处的货时，*差点*把整排泡面堆碰倒，唐在门口默默鼓起了掌。
almost:0.hook: Tang said it had fallen before, and the story was much worse.
almost:0.line: 'I *almost* dropped the whole shelf on my first week here — welcome to the club.'

especially:0.en: Weekend nights brought a different kind of crowd, *especially* after midnight when the last buses stopped running. Students with nowhere to go would sit by the magazine rack, not really reading, just warm and quiet. The Manager never rushed them out. She would simply brew a fresh pot of tea and leave it on the counter without a word.
especially:0.cnHint: 周末夜里来店里的人特别多，____是末班车停运之后，有些学生会在杂志架旁坐很久。
especially:0.hook: One of them left a folded note under the tea pot.
especially:0.line: 'Weekend nights are busy — *especially* after the last bus goes.'

publish:0.en: A man in a wrinkled coat came in and bought three pens and a thick notebook. He told me, with great seriousness, that he was going to *publish* a collection of short stories before the year was out. I said that sounded wonderful. He nodded, tucked the notebook under his arm, and walked straight into the closed glass door on his way out.
publish:0.cnHint: 一位穿皱外套的男士买了笔和本子，严肃地告诉我他今年内要____一本短篇小说集。
publish:0.hook: He came back the next night and bought two more pens.
publish:0.line: 'I plan to *publish* my first book before the snow comes — no more waiting.'

activity:0.en: The Manager pinned a hand-drawn poster to the door: WEEKEND LUCKY DRAW — BUY ANY THREE ITEMS TO JOIN. 'A store needs *activity* or it gets forgotten,' she said, pressing the last piece of tape down firmly. By ten o'clock the rubbish bin was full of small torn tickets, and one very calm old man was holding the winning stub and asking what he had won.
activity:0.cnHint: 店长在门上贴了手绘的抽奖海报，说店里需要这样的____才不会被人忘记。
activity:0.hook: The prize was a single bag of rice crackers, and he seemed genuinely delighted.
activity:0.line: 'A store needs *activity* — a lucky draw is the easiest way to start.'

science:0.en: Lin stopped by late on Saturday, arms full of textbooks. She dropped one on the counter by mistake and it fell open to a chapter on plant cells. 'Don't ask,' she said, before I could speak. Apparently her study group had decided that *science* was easier to understand at three in the morning with convenience-store coffee and low expectations.
science:0.cnHint: 林深夜抱着一堆课本进来，其中一本翻到了植物细胞那章——看来她的学习小组觉得用____在凌晨三点开搞也没什么问题。
science:0.hook: She bought four coffees, which meant at least three other people were waiting somewhere nearby.
science:0.line: '*Science* at midnight sounds terrible, but here we are — four coffees please.'

receive:0.en: The store phone rang just after midnight. I picked it up, a little nervous. 'You'll *receive* a big delivery at one a.m.,' the Manager said. 'Sign everything carefully.' Ten boxes arrived exactly on time, each one sealed with bright orange tape. The last box had no label at all.
receive:0.cnHint: 午夜刚过，店长打来电话说我们将____一批货，但最后一个箱子没有任何标签。
receive:0.hook: No label, no sender — just a faint ticking sound inside.
receive:0.line: 'You'll *receive* the boxes soon, so clear some space now.'

encourage:0.en: Tang noticed I was slow at counting change during the rush. Instead of laughing, she leaned over and smiled. 'You're doing fine,' she said. Her words *encouraged* me enough to keep going without a single mistake for the rest of the night. By dawn she was gone, but she had left a small note by the register.
encourage:0.cnHint: 阿糖看到我找零很慢，用温暖的话语____了我，还在收银台旁留下了一张小纸条。
encourage:0.hook: The note said only: 'Ask me about the Tuesday regular.'
encourage:0.line: 'I want to *encourage* you — everyone gets faster with time.'

travel:0.en: An old man came in at three a.m. with a big backpack and mud on his boots. He bought two bottles of water and a map. 'Long *travel* ahead?' I asked. He laughed quietly. 'I've been walking the same road for thirty years,' he said. He paid in exact coins and left without waiting for his receipt.
travel:0.cnHint: 一位背着大包的老人深夜来买水和地图，说他的____已经持续了三十年。
travel:0.hook: His name on the loyalty card matched the store's very first receipt.
travel:0.line: 'A long *travel* starts with a good bottle of water, young one.'

strong:0.en: The wind outside was *strong* enough to shake the front windows. I was stacking cans when one rolled off and hit the floor with a loud bang. A woman in a yellow coat pushed the door open without any trouble at all, as if the storm was nothing. She bought hot soup and sat by the window, watching the street.
strong:0.cnHint: 窗外狂风____，一位穿黄色外套的女人毫不费力地推门而入，买了热汤坐下来望着街道。
strong:0.hook: She watched one particular shadow across the street without blinking.
strong:0.line: 'The wind is *strong* tonight, but I like it that way.'

chance:0.en: Lin walked in holding a stack of flyers from the shop next door. She looked around, then slipped one under a bag of chips when she thought I wasn't looking. I cleared my throat. She froze. 'Any *chance* you'll let that go?' she asked with a careful smile. I handed the flyer back without a word.
chance:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林悄悄把对手店的传单塞进货架，被我发现后问我有没有____放她一马。
chance:0.hook: She came back an hour later — this time carrying two cups of tea.
chance:0.line: 'Any *chance* we could just forget this happened?'

solve:0.en: The card reader stopped working at two a.m. A line of tired customers waited. I tried restarting it three times. Then Tang texted from home: 'Unplug the blue wire, count to five, plug it back.' I did. It worked. 'How did she *solve* it so fast?' one customer asked. I just smiled and said, 'Experience.'
solve:0.cnHint: 读卡机深夜突然罢工，阿糖发短信教我如何____这个问题，顾客们都惊讶不已。
solve:0.hook: Tang's text had been sent six minutes before the machine even broke.
solve:0.line: 'I can *solve* most problems in this store with one blue wire.'

quite:0.en: The Manager stopped by at four a.m. for his usual coffee check. He looked at my tidy shelves and the clean floor and said nothing for a long moment. 'Not bad,' he said at last. Coming from him, that was *quite* a compliment — Tang had warned me he gave praise about twice a year. He refilled his cup and left.
quite:0.cnHint: 店长凌晨来巡查，对我整洁的货架说了句"不错"，阿糖说这____是难得的夸奖。
quite:0.hook: He paused at the door and added, 'Watch the man in seat three.'
quite:0.line: 'That shelf is *quite* clean — better than last week's effort.'

technology:0.en: A teenage boy spent twenty minutes trying to pay with his phone, but the app kept failing. 'I love *technology*,' he muttered sadly. I pointed to the small card reader on the counter. He tapped his card and it worked in one second. He stared at the reader as if he had never noticed it before, then laughed at himself.
technology:0.cnHint: 一个少年抱怨____让他的手机支付一直失败，却没想到刷卡机一秒就解决了问题。
technology:0.hook: He left his phone number on a receipt — 'for tech support,' he wrote.
technology:0.line: 'I trust *technology* — I just don't trust my phone battery.'

education:0.en: The Manager tapped the noticeboard above the coffee machine. 'Every new clerk reads this,' he said. It listed everything from how to greet customers to how to mop the floor. My *education* as a night-shift clerk had officially begun, one laminated rule at a time.
education:0.cnHint: 店长指着公告栏，告诉我这就是我的____从这里开始。
education:0.hook: But rule number seven had been crossed out by someone.
education:0.line: 'Your *education* starts tonight — read every word on that board.'

scientist:0.en: A quiet woman in a white coat came in every night at two for a bottle of warm tea. Tang whispered that she worked at the research centre nearby. 'She once explained her whole project to me,' Tang said. 'I understood nothing.' The *scientist* smiled at me like she already knew that.
scientist:0.cnHint: 那位____每晚两点准时来买热茶，同事说她来自附近的研究中心。
scientist:0.hook: Tonight she bought two bottles and looked strangely nervous.
scientist:0.line: 'Even a *scientist* needs a quiet cup of tea at two in the morning.'

physical:0.en: Lin arrived pushing a trolley loaded with energy drinks and protein bars. 'Big gym sale next door,' Lin explained with a grin. The *physical* effort of lifting all those heavy boxes onto the counter made Lin breathe hard. I offered a bag. Lin refused, flexed once, and walked out.
physical:0.cnHint: 林扛着一堆运动补给品来结账，这份____上的考验让他气喘吁吁。
physical:0.hook: The trolley he left behind had someone else's name tag on it.
physical:0.line: 'All this *physical* work deserves a free sports drink, don't you think?'

quality:0.en: A grandmother held a small toy rabbit under the store light, turning it slowly. 'I always check before I buy,' she told me. She pressed the ears, pulled the tail, and read the label twice. '*Quality* matters when it is a gift for a child,' she said, then set it gently back on the shelf.
quality:0.cnHint: 一位老奶奶在灯下仔细检查玩具兔子，说送给孩子的礼物____很重要。
quality:0.hook: She left empty-handed, whispering a name I could not catch.
quality:0.line: '*Quality* matters most when the gift is for someone small and trusting.'

habit:0.en: Every night at midnight, Tang made two cups of instant noodles — one for himself and one left on the counter, just in case. 'Old *habit*,' Tang shrugged when I asked. 'Started when a hungry student came in with no money.' I looked at the spare cup. It was already gone.
habit:0.cnHint: 同事每晚定时煮两碗泡面，这个____背后有一个温暖的故事。
habit:0.hook: The student had never come back, Tang said — until last Tuesday.
habit:0.line: 'It is just a *habit*, but it has never once gone to waste.'

sound:0.en: At three in the morning the store was perfectly still. Then a soft, repeated knock came from the back near the drinks fridge. I froze. Tang did not even look up. 'Loose pipe,' he said calmly. The *sound* faded, then returned, steady as a slow heartbeat behind the shelves.
sound:0.cnHint: 深夜三点，冰柜附近传来奇怪的____，把我吓了一跳。
sound:0.hook: Tang's calm expression lasted exactly until the second knock came.
sound:0.line: 'That *sound* has been there for a week — the Manager says ignore it.'

average:0.en: Lin leaned on the counter studying a printed chart. 'My store sells thirty cups of coffee a day,' Lin announced. 'What is your *average*?' I checked our log: forty-two. I said nothing and just refilled the machine. Lin stared at the chart for a long moment, then folded it very slowly.
average:0.cnHint: 林拿着销售图表来比较咖啡日____，结果有些尴尬。
average:0.hook: Lin came back an hour later and asked to see our exact numbers.
average:0.line: 'My daily *average* is thirty — what does your little store manage?'

body:0.en: After the long weekend rush, I finally sat down. Every part of me ached. Tang handed me a warm can of soup without a word. 'You have to take care of your *body* on this shift,' he said quietly. 'The store never closes, but you are not a machine.' I held the can with both hands.
body:0.cnHint: 漫长的促销夜班结束后，同事递来热汤，提醒我要照顾好自己的____。
body:0.hook: Then his phone buzzed and his whole face changed colour.
body:0.line: 'Take care of your *body* first — a tired clerk makes costly mistakes.'

personal:0.en: The Manager pinned a new chart to the wall before my shift began. It listed every clerk's sales numbers — no hiding behind team totals. 'This is *personal*,' Tang whispered, pointing at the tiny number beside my name. I laughed, but I did start straightening the snack display a little faster after that.
personal:0.cnHint: 店长把每个店员的销售数字贴在墙上，我的____数据让同事觉得有点尴尬。
personal:0.hook: Tang's own number was circled in red — and not by the Manager.
personal:0.line: 'This chart makes every mistake *personal*, so be careful out there.'

rather:0.en: A regular came in just before two in the morning, studied the hot-food shelf for a long time, and then bought a single cup of instant noodles. I thought she would take a seat by the window, but she stood at the counter instead. She seemed *rather* lonely, though she was smiling the whole time.
rather:0.cnHint: 一位深夜常客买了泡面，看起来____孤独，却一直微笑着。
rather:0.hook: She left her phone number on the receipt — but it was not meant for me.
rather:0.line: 'It is *rather* late to be shopping alone, don't you think?'

instead:0.en: Tang forgot to reorder the weekend rice balls, so the shelf sat empty all Saturday morning. Customers kept reaching for the spot and pulling their hands back with a frown. The Manager did not scold Tang; she put up a cheerful sign offering warm dumplings *instead*. Every single dumpling sold out by noon.
instead:0.cnHint: 饭团缺货，店长没有责怪同事，而是用另一种食物____代替，结果卖光了。
instead:0.hook: Tang has been suspiciously cheerful about dumplings ever since.
instead:0.line: 'Take the dumplings *instead* — trust me, they are better anyway.'

performance:0.en: The Manager called a short meeting before the Saturday rush. She said last weekend's *performance* — slow checkouts, a messy aisle, two wrong change — had cost us three stars on the neighbourhood review board. Tang looked at the floor. I looked at Tang. Nobody said anything for a moment.
performance:0.cnHint: 店长开会指出上周末的____不理想，三项失误让评分下降了。
performance:0.hook: The third mistake on that list was mine, and I had hoped no one noticed.
performance:0.line: 'Your *performance* this weekend will decide the store rating, no pressure.'

percent:0.en: A handwritten sign near the register read: 'Weekend members save ten *percent*.' An old man squinted at it, pulled out a membership card so worn I could barely read the number, and placed it on the counter with great ceremony. He bought one pack of mints. He seemed very satisfied.
percent:0.cnHint: 会员可以享受____折扣，一位老人郑重地用破旧会员卡买了一包薄荷糖。
percent:0.hook: That card expired two years ago, but I decided some battles are not worth fighting.
percent:0.line: 'Ten *percent* off sounds small until you come here every single day.'

achieve:0.en: Lin from the store across the street walked in during the quiet afternoon lull and browsed every aisle slowly. I watched from behind the register. Finally she bought a cold drink and said, quite pleasantly, 'Nice layout.' I had rearranged those shelves myself that morning, trying to *achieve* the tidy look the Manager always described.
achieve:0.cnHint: 竞争对手进店参观，而我正努力____店长一直描述的那种整洁效果。
achieve:0.hook: Lin took three photos before she left, and she thought I wasn't looking.
achieve:0.line: 'Hard work is the only way to *achieve* something worth copying.'

challenge:0.en: Saturday night brought a sudden crowd — a street event had just ended nearby. The line reached the door, every basket was full, and the card reader blinked a warning light. Tang mouthed 'good luck' from across the counter. I took a breath. A busy rush is only a *challenge* if you let it feel like one.
challenge:0.cnHint: 周末夜晚人潮涌来，收款机也亮起警告灯，这真是一个不小的____。
challenge:0.hook: The card reader fixed itself, but only after the longest thirty seconds of my life.
challenge:0.line: 'Every big crowd is a *challenge*, but that is also how you learn fast.'

power:0.en: Just after midnight the streetlight outside flickered and died, and for one second I thought the whole store would lose *power* too. The fridge hummed on, the lights stayed bright, and a sleepy cat on the step outside didn't even twitch. Tang patted the counter and said the store had never gone dark in three years.
power:0.cnHint: 午夜路灯突然灭了，我担心店里也会断____，好在什么都没发生。
power:0.hook: Tang knocked on wood after saying that, very quietly, hoping I wouldn't notice.
power:0.line: 'As long as we have *power*, this store is open — rain, wind, or worse.'

key:0.en: The Manager handed me a small metal ring on my first night. 'This is the *key* to the back storage room,' he said, 'but also the key to understanding how this store works — learn what is inside, and you will know everything.' I clipped it to my belt and felt, oddly, like I had just been trusted with something important.
key:0.cnHint: 店长把储藏室的____交给我，说读懂它就读懂了这家店。
key:0.hook: But the storage room held more than shelves of instant noodles.
key:0.line: 'This *key* opens the room, but it also opens a few secrets.'

issue:0.en: Tang slid a thin magazine across the counter. 'New *issue* just arrived,' she whispered, like it was treasure. She came every week for this small cooking magazine, always reading the first page before she even paid. Tonight she paused at one article longer than usual, her finger tracing a recipe she clearly already knew by heart.
issue:0.cnHint: 唐每周都来取她最喜欢的杂志新____，今晚她在某一页上停留了很久。
issue:0.hook: She tore out that one page and tucked it carefully into her coat pocket.
issue:0.line: 'Is this week's *issue* in yet? I have been waiting since Monday.'

against:0.en: The rain came suddenly. A young woman pressed herself *against* the glass door, shaking water from her hair, then stepped inside with an apologetic smile. She bought nothing — just stood near the warm drink shelf for ten minutes, breathing slowly. I pretended to recount the chewing gum so she could stay a little longer without feeling awkward.
against:0.cnHint: 一位年轻女士冒雨靠____玻璃门，进店后只是静静地站在暖饮架旁。
against:0.hook: She came back the next three nights, always just before midnight.
against:0.line: 'Sorry — can I lean *against* your wall for just a moment? The rain is awful.'

matter:0.en: Lin came in just after two in the morning looking tired. I asked if everything was okay. 'Small *matter*,' she said, waving her hand. She bought a warm can of corn soup, sat on the step outside, and stayed there for a long time, staring at the empty street. Whatever the matter was, it did not feel small to me.
matter:0.cnHint: 林深夜来买热汤，说只是一件小____，却在门口台阶上坐了很久。
matter:0.hook: She left without finishing the soup, which she had never done before.
matter:0.line: 'It is no big *matter* — I just needed some air and somewhere quiet.'

raise:0.en: I noticed the shelf for the small local honey jars was always empty by Thursday. The Manager explained that an old man raised bees on the hill behind town and brought one box each week. 'He used to *raise* three boxes,' the Manager said quietly, 'before his wife passed.' The honey sold out in hours, every single time.
raise:0.cnHint: 店长说，山上有位老人____蜂为生，每周送来一小箱蜂蜜。

whole:0.en: Just before dawn the street went perfectly quiet. I looked out at the empty corner, the wet pavement catching the light, and felt something settle inside me. variety:0.line: 'We have a wide *variety* of snacks on sale today!'

gain:0.cnHint: 忙过午夜高峰后，我感觉自己____了不少自信，店长默默放了杯热茶在我旁边。

maybe:0.en: A man stood at the drink fridge for a long time, opening and closing the glass door. '*Maybe* the green tea,' he said quietly to himself, then put it back. He picked up a lemon water, then a barley drink. I pretended to tidy a shelf nearby so I would not make him feel watched.
maybe:0.cnHint: 一位男士在饮料柜前反复拿起又放下，口中喃喃说着____要绿茶。

maybe:0.line: '*Maybe* the green tea is the right choice after all.'

huge:0.en: A *huge* delivery arrived at the back door just as the sale hit its busiest hour. Tang and I unloaded box after box while the Manager handled the front counter alone. huge:0.cnHint: 促销最忙的时候，后门来了一批____的货，我和阿糖一箱箱往里搬。
huge:0.hook: One box was labeled with a name none of us recognised.
huge:0.line: 'That is a *huge* amount of stock for one night!'

diet:0.en: A regular customer, an older woman, studied every label carefully before placing anything in her basket. diet:0.cnHint: 一位老顾客仔细查看每件商品的标签，因为医生给她制定了严格的____计划。
diet:0.hook: She paused at one small packet for a very long time.

animal:0.en: The Manager set up a small display near the door for the weekend sale. Someone had left a tiny toy *animal* — a fat little bear — on top of the stack of discount chips. Nobody claimed it. I put it on the counter, and every customer who walked in smiled at it without meaning to.
animal:0.cnHint: 促销周末，收银台上摆着一只无人认领的玩具____，每个进店的顾客看到它都会不自觉地微笑。
animal:0.hook: Then one customer stopped, stared, and went very quiet.

goal:0.cnHint: 阿糖在冰柜门上贴了一张纸，写着本周末的销售____，快到午夜时已经完成了大半。
goal:0.hook: At 11:58, a stranger walked in and bought thirteen cups at once.

adult:0.en: A kid of about ten came in alone, carefully counting coins on the counter. He was one yuan short for the drink he wanted. I looked around — no *adult* with him. I told him the drink was on special today. He nodded very seriously and said, 'I will pay the rest next time.' He meant it.
adult:0.cnHint: 一个小男孩独自来买饮料，差一块钱，店里没有____陪同，店员帮了他。
adult:0.hook: He came back an hour later — but not alone.

poor:0.en: The weekend rush left the shelves looking *poor* — gaps everywhere, torn price tags, one lonely can of soup facing the wrong way. I spent twenty quiet minutes putting everything back in order. When the Manager arrived at dawn, she stopped, looked around, and simply nodded once.
poor:0.cnHint: 周末客流过后，货架变得空空荡荡、乱糟糟的，店员花时间把一切整理好了。
poor:0.hook: The Manager's nod hid something she had not said yet.

type:0.en: A woman spent ten minutes in the snack aisle, picking up each bag and putting it back. Finally she came to me and asked what *type* of chip was the most popular. I said the spicy one. She bought the plain one. I have decided that is completely fine.

sense:0.cnHint: 午夜人流散去后，店员感受到一种平静的____，阿糖也注意到了。

rate:0.cnHint: 阿糖给店员看了周末销售____的数据，上涨了三十个百分点，店长的反应很有意思。
rate:0.hook: The Manager paused at the door, then turned back to say one more thing.
rate:0.line: 'The sales *rate* is up thirty percent — the Manager will be happy.'

action:0.cnHint: 周末促销让小店热闹非凡，阿糖建议最好的____就是保持微笑。
action:0.hook: The old man in the rain coat came back an hour later for something else.
action:0.line: 'The best *action* right now is to keep smiling.'

situation:0.line: 'Interesting *situation*, right? Good thing I planned ahead.'

member:0.cnHint: 一位____资格的常客悄悄拿走了我们都惦记着的最后一份冷藏甜品。

heart:0.en: By three in the morning the store was quiet and the sale banners hung still. Lin came in from the cold, dropped a bag of unsold goods on the counter, and sighed. heart:0.cnHint: 凌晨三点，林走进店里，说了一句关于促销____的话，然后露出一个奇怪的微笑。

disease:0.line: 'A *disease* is spreading through our whole team fast.'

mind:0.en: The weekend sale brought a rush of customers. I lost count of the snack orders and mixed up two bags. Tang laughed and said a sharp *mind* was the most useful tool behind the counter. I nodded, quietly deciding to make a checklist for next time.

mind:0.hook: Then Tang slid a small notebook across the counter toward me.
mind:0.line: 'A sharp *mind* is the best tool you have back here.'

rise:0.en: By ten o'clock, the line at the register showed no sign of getting shorter. The Manager watched the sales screen and gave a quiet smile. 'A *rise* like this only happens twice a year,' he said, almost to himself. I stacked cups faster and tried to keep up with the pace.

prove:0.en: The new electronic shelf labels kept changing price on their own. Customers pointed, confused. I checked each one carefully and found a loose wire at the back. Tang said anyone could *prove* their worth on a night like this, and I felt a small glow of pride as I fixed the last label.

maintain:0.hook: Lin lingered by the door far longer than a coffee run required.
maintain:0.line: 'Hard to *maintain* a dry floor on a night like this, isn't it?'

worker:0.en: The weekend sale turned the store into a small storm. Every shelf needed restocking, every counter needed wiping. I was moving so fast I almost knocked over Tang. 'You look like a real *worker* now,' Tang said, laughing. I didn't feel like one — I just felt lost.
worker:0.cnHint: 促销活动让我忙得团团转，同事夸我是个真正的____。
worker:0.hook: Then Tang's smile faded, eyes fixed on the door.
worker:0.line: 'You look like a real *worker* now,' Tang said.

control:0.en: Customers kept grabbing the last bottles of juice off the shelf before I could arrange them neatly. I tried to *control* the flow by standing near the display and smiling politely. It worked for about two minutes. Then someone knocked the whole row over and the bottles rolled everywhere.
control:0.cnHint: 我试图____顾客拿货的节奏，结果却更乱了。
control:0.hook: One bottle rolled behind the counter and hit something that beeped.
control:0.line: 'I need to *control* this shelf or everything falls apart.'

product:0.en: The Manager had placed a new *product* right at the entrance — a small jar of honey from a local farm. Customers stopped, picked it up, turned it over, smiled. By nine in the morning, half the jars were gone. I hadn't even seen the Manager put them there.
product:0.cnHint: 店长悄悄在入口摆了一款新____，顾客们纷纷驻足。
product:0.hook: The last jar had a handwritten note tucked underneath it.
product:0.line: 'This *product* comes from a farm just down the road,' the Manager said.

practice:0.en: Before the rush hit, Tang showed me the quick-scan *practice* every clerk learns: left hand steadies the item, right hand sweeps the scanner, eyes check the screen. 'Three seconds per item,' Tang said. I tried it ten times until it felt smooth. Then the line of customers arrived.
practice:0.cnHint: 同事在促销前教我收银的____，让我提前熟悉流程。
practice:0.hook: The very first customer placed forty-seven items on the counter.
practice:0.line: 'It just takes *practice* — you will get it fast,' Tang said.

environment:0.en: The store felt different during the sale. Bright signs, extra lights, music from a small speaker near the window. I paused for a second and looked around. The whole *environment* felt alive, almost like a little festival. Then I noticed Lin watching me from across the street through the glass.
environment:0.cnHint: 促销布置让店里的____焕然一新，我感觉自己身处小节日中。
environment:0.hook: Lin had not moved in ten minutes, just watching.
environment:0.line: 'I really like the *environment* we've created in here today,' Tang said.

system:0.en: The checkout *system* crashed at half past ten. The screen froze, the scanner beeped twice, and the queue grew long. The Manager stayed completely calm, pulled out a small notebook, and wrote prices by hand. 'Old ways still work,' the Manager said quietly. I was not so calm.
system:0.cnHint: 收银____突然崩溃，店长拿出小本子用老办法顶了上去。
system:0.hook: The notebook had prices I had never seen on any shelf.
system:0.line: 'The *system* is down, but we keep going,' the Manager said quietly.

natural:0.en: A small girl came in with her grandfather. She walked straight to the snack shelf, then stopped and put everything back without being told. The grandfather smiled at me. 'It is *natural* for her,' he said softly. 'She helps at home too.' They bought only a bottle of water and left slowly.
natural:0.cnHint: 一个小女孩____地把零食放回货架，让爷爷骄傲地笑了。
natural:0.hook: The grandfather paused at the door and glanced back once.
natural:0.line: 'It is *natural* for her — she always puts things back,' he said.

free:0.en: At eleven, the Manager taped a small sign near the coffee machine: one cup *free* with any purchase over thirty yuan. The queue doubled in two minutes. Tang looked at me. I looked at Tang. Neither of us knew how to use the coffee machine. The Manager had already left the room.
free:0.cnHint: 店长贴出满额____咖啡的告示，我和同事面面相觑不知如何操作。
free:0.hook: From the back room came the sound of the Manager laughing softly.
free:0.line: 'One cup *free* — that sign was the Manager's idea,' Tang whispered.

compare:1.en: Saturday morning, a big sale sign went up outside the store. Lin stood across the street, notebook in hand, writing down our prices. I watched her *compare* our snack wall with her own shop's display, frowning each time our numbers were lower. The Manager noticed too, and smiled quietly.
compare:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在街对面，把我们的价格和她自己店里的____，皱着眉头。
compare:1.hook: Lin tucked her notebook away and made one phone call.
compare:1.line: 'I always *compare* prices before I change mine,' Lin said coolly.

past:1.en: Just after midnight, an old man shuffled *past* the store window every single night without stopping. Tonight, for the first time, he paused at the door and looked at the sale posters. His eyes went soft, like he was remembering something. I held my breath and waited to see if he would come in.
past:1.cnHint: 一位老人每晚都从店门口走____，今晚却第一次停下来望着橱窗。
past:1.hook: He touched the glass once, then turned and walked away.
past:1.line: 'I used to walk *past* this corner every day as a boy,' he said softly.

suffer:1.en: A young woman sat on the bench outside, rubbing her feet after the morning street sale. 'These shoes are killing me,' she groaned. She had clearly been standing in line for hours and was beginning to *suffer* for a good deal on a rice cooker. I brought her a small stool from inside.
suffer:1.cnHint: 一位年轻女士在外面的长椅上坐下，因为长时间排队而____着脚痛。
suffer:1.hook: She thanked me, then asked if we sold any plasters.
suffer:1.line: 'Nobody should *suffer* this much just to save twenty yuan,' she laughed.

almost:1.en: The outdoor sale cart was piled so high that it *almost* blocked the whole pavement. Shoppers squeezed past sideways, bags knocking together like bumper cars at a fair. The Manager kept rearranging things to make more room, but somehow the pile only got bigger. I started to worry about the fire exit.
almost:1.cnHint: 促销推车堆得太高，____把整条人行道都堵住了。
almost:1.hook: Then someone sneezed, and the top layer began to wobble.
almost:1.line: 'It *almost* fell on a customer just now!' I whispered to Tang.

especially:1.en: The street outside was loud all morning, *especially* when the noodle cart next door started playing its jingle on repeat. Shoppers paused, tapping their feet without realising it. Tang said the noise was actually good for business because happy feet meant open wallets. I was not sure that was real science, but sales did go up.
especially:1.cnHint: 街上整个上午都很吵，____是隔壁面条摊开始循环播放广告曲之后。
especially:1.hook: At noon the jingle suddenly stopped, and everyone looked around.
especially:1.line: 'I like weekend crowds, *especially* the snack rush,' Tang told me.

publish:1.en: A man set up a small folding table near our entrance and began to *publish* a free neighbourhood newsletter, handing fresh copies to every shopper who walked past. He said it was issue one. One headline read: 'Local Store Holds Biggest Sale of the Year.' The Manager came out, read it, and shook his hand warmly.
publish:1.cnHint: 一位男士在店门口摆摊，____他自己制作的免费社区小报，头版写的是我们的促销。
publish:1.hook: Inside his bag I spotted a second headline, not yet printed.
publish:1.line: 'I *publish* it myself every Saturday morning,' the man said proudly.

activity:1.en: By nine in the morning the outdoor sale had become the loudest *activity* on the whole street. Kids chased each other between the display tables while their parents argued cheerfully over discounted instant noodles. The Manager stood in the middle of it all, clapping his hands like a referee at a friendly match. Tang and I just tried to keep up.
activity:1.cnHint: 户外促销成了整条街上最热闹的____，孩子们在展示桌间追逐嬉闹。
activity:1.hook: Then a small dog joined the chase, and things got complicated.
activity:1.line: 'This *activity* is good for the whole neighbourhood,' the Manager beamed.

science:1.en: A girl no older than twelve stopped outside, staring at a display of experiment kits marked down for the sale. She picked up each box, reading the back carefully. 'This is real *science*,' she told her grandmother, eyes wide. Her grandmother sighed, checked the price tag, and then nodded slowly. The girl's face lit up like a lamp.
science:1.cnHint: 一个小女孩在打折的实验套装前驻足，认真地告诉奶奶这是真正的____。
science:1.hook: She came back twenty minutes later, alone, with exact change.
science:1.line: '*Science* is the only thing I want for my birthday,' she said firmly.

contribute:1.en: The Manager dragged a folding table onto the pavement outside and piled it with sale items. He asked every passing neighbour to *contribute* one old item from home for a swap corner. Most people laughed, then came back ten minutes later with something tucked under their arm.
contribute:1.cnHint: 店长在店外摆了一张桌子，邀请街坊____旧物，搞起了一个交换角。
contribute:1.hook: One neighbour's 'old item' turned out to have someone's name written inside.
contribute:1.line: 'Everyone should *contribute* something — even one pen counts,' the Manager said.

share:1.en: Tang split a meat bun in two and handed half across the counter to me without a word. 'Night shifts are long,' she said. That small *share* of a warm bun at two in the morning felt better than any meal I had eaten all week.
share:1.cnHint: 唐把一个肉包分成两半，把那____递给了我——这是我这周吃过最温暖的东西。
share:1.hook: Tang had been splitting that same bun every night for a reason she hadn't told anyone.
share:1.line: 'Here — your *share*. You looked hungry an hour ago,' Tang said.

decade:1.en: A white-haired man stood outside reading the sale poster for a full minute. 'I have come to this corner for a *decade*,' he told me through the open door, 'and I have never once seen a real discount.' He bought three bags of chips anyway.
decade:1.cnHint: 一位老先生站在门外说，他来这个路口已经____了，从没见过真正的折扣。
decade:1.hook: He slipped a small photograph onto the counter before he left.
decade:1.line: 'I have walked past this corner for a *decade* and you still surprise me,' he said.

kind:1.en: I could not decide which *kind* of tea to put in the front basket for the sale. The Manager said to watch which shelf customers touched first when they walked in. By midnight I had a clear answer — and it was not the one he expected.
kind:1.cnHint: 我不知道该把哪____茶放在促销篮里，店长让我观察顾客进门后先摸哪里。
kind:1.hook: The most popular choice had been discontinued three months ago.
kind:1.line: 'What *kind* of tea do people actually want?' I asked the Manager.

across:1.en: A girl on a bicycle stopped *across* the street and stared at our sale banner for a long moment. Then she crossed over, locked her bike to the lamp post, and walked in with a very specific shopping list written on the back of her hand.
across:1.cnHint: 一个骑自行车的女孩停在街道____，盯着我们的促销横幅看了很久，然后过来了。
across:1.hook: The list on her hand was written in someone else's handwriting.
across:1.line: 'I spotted your sign from *across* the street — are the prices real?' she asked.

factor:1.en: Tang told me the biggest *factor* in a good night-shift sale was not the discount but the smell — warm food near the door pulled people in faster than any poster. She switched on the small oven at eleven and proved it within twenty minutes.
factor:1.cnHint: 唐告诉我，夜间促销最重要的____不是折扣，而是气味。
factor:1.hook: She learned that trick at a different store she never talks about.
factor:1.line: 'Smell is the biggest *factor*. Watch the door after I turn this on,' Tang said.

condition:1.en: The Manager read out the sale rules to me from a card: every item at half price on one *condition* — the customer had to name the item in English. He winked. Half his regulars had been practising English phrases all week without knowing why.
condition:1.cnHint: 店长宣布促销有一个____：顾客必须用英语说出商品名称，这让不少熟客悄悄练了一周英语。
condition:1.hook: One regular had been carrying a tiny notebook of English words every night for days.
condition:1.line: 'Half price on one *condition* — say the name in English,' the Manager announced.

effort:1.en: I spent an hour arranging the window display for the sale, taping little price signs at neat angles. The Manager glanced at it, nodded once, and said nothing. Tang leaned over and whispered that one silent nod was the most *effort* he ever gave with praise.
effort:1.cnHint: 我花了一个小时布置橱窗，店长只是点了一下头——唐说那已经是他____最多的表扬了。
effort:1.hook: Tang had been waiting two years for a nod like that herself.
effort:1.line: 'That nod is real *effort* from him — do not take it lightly,' Tang whispered.

education:1.en: The street outside the store was loud with a weekend crowd. A woman set up a small table and began teaching children how to count coins. 'This is *education* you can use every day,' she told them. The Manager watched from the doorway, arms crossed, nodding slowly.
education:1.cnHint: 一位女士在店门外摆了张桌子，给孩子们做____，店长在门口静静地看着。
education:1.hook: The Manager stepped outside, and his expression was hard to read.
education:1.line: 'This is *education* you can use every day.'

scientist:1.en: A man in a dusty coat stopped in front of the store window and stared at the snack display for a very long time. Tang leaned over the counter and whispered, 'He does that every Saturday.' The man turned, smiled, and said he was a *scientist* who studied why people choose one snack over another.
scientist:1.cnHint: 一个穿旧外套的男人盯着零食看了很久，唐悄悄说他其实是个____。
scientist:1.hook: He pulled out a small notebook and began writing something down.
scientist:1.line: 'I am a *scientist* who studies why people choose snacks.'

physical:1.en: Lin arrived before sunrise to hang sale signs along the front of the store. By the time I unlocked the door, she was already out of breath. 'The *physical* work is the part nobody warns you about,' she said, rubbing her shoulders. She still managed to smile and wave at the first customer.
physical:1.cnHint: 林天亮前就来挂促销牌子，做完____上的劳累活儿后，她揉着肩膀笑着迎接第一位顾客。
physical:1.hook: Lin winked at me as the customer walked in carrying something unusual.
physical:1.line: 'The *physical* work is the part nobody warns you about.'

quality:1.en: A couple stopped outside and argued quietly over which rice wine to buy. The man kept pointing at the cheaper bottle. The woman shook her head and said, '*Quality* matters more than price.' They came inside together, still debating, and placed both bottles on the counter in front of me.
quality:1.cnHint: 一对情侣在店外为选哪瓶米酒争论，女方坚持____比价格更重要。
quality:1.hook: Neither of them could agree, so they both looked at me for the answer.
quality:1.line: '*Quality* matters more than price, trust me.'

habit:1.en: Every Saturday morning, an old man walked one slow lap around the block before stopping at our store for a small carton of warm soy milk. 'It is a *habit* from forty years ago,' he told me today, setting his coins on the counter with great care. The Manager gave him a small bow.
habit:1.cnHint: 一位老先生每周六都要绕街区走一圈再来买豆浆，他说这个____已经保持了四十年。
habit:1.hook: This Saturday, the old man arrived with a young boy beside him.
habit:1.line: 'It is a *habit* I have kept for forty years.'

sound:1.en: The delivery truck arrived at six in the morning and the *sound* of rolling crates echoed down the quiet street, waking two cats on the steps next door. Tang and I worked fast, stacking boxes before the first shoppers arrived. One of the crates was sealed with extra tape and had no label at all.
sound:1.cnHint: 送货车清晨到来，货箱滚动的____把街上的猫都惊醒了，唐和我赶紧搬货。
sound:1.hook: That unmarked crate was not on any list I could find.
sound:1.line: 'That *sound* will wake the whole street every time.'

average:1.en: Lin printed a sign showing that our weekend rice was thirty percent cheaper than the *average* price on the street. She taped it to the lamp post just outside the door and then stood back to admire it. Within five minutes, a small line had formed on the pavement.
average:1.cnHint: 林打印了一张告示，说我们的米价比街上的____价格低三成，贴出去没多久就排起了队。
average:1.hook: The owner of the shop across the street came out and stared at the sign.
average:1.line: 'Our price is well below the *average* on this street.'

body:1.en: A young man sat down on the low wall outside, head drooping, backpack still on his shoulders. He looked as if his whole *body* had run out of energy. I brought him a small cup of hot tea on my break. He looked up, surprised, and said he had been standing at a job fair all morning.
body:1.cnHint: 一个年轻人坐在店外的矮墙上，整个____都透着疲惫，我端了杯热茶出去给他。
body:1.hook: He reached into his backpack and handed me a folded piece of paper.
body:1.line: 'My whole *body* just stopped working after that job fair.'

personal:1.en: Saturday morning. The Manager stood outside the store, taping a big sale sign to the window. A woman stopped and asked him to move so she could read it. 'This is my *personal* project,' he said proudly, spreading his arms wide to block her view even more.
personal:1.cnHint: 店长在店外贴促销海报，却用自己的身体挡住了路人的视线。
personal:1.hook: The woman pulled out her phone and started filming.
personal:1.line: This sign is my *personal* masterpiece, and I will not move.

rather:1.en: Outside the store, Tang was handing out discount flyers. Most people walked past without taking one. A little boy stopped, looked at the flyer, then looked up at Tang. 'I would *rather* have a sticker,' the boy said. Tang stared. She had nothing else to give.
rather:1.cnHint: 唐在门口派发传单，一个小男孩却说他____要贴纸。
rather:1.hook: Then Tang noticed a sticker on her own jacket sleeve.
rather:1.line: I would *rather* have something fun, not a piece of paper.

instead:1.en: Lin had set up a small table outside his own shop across the street, offering free samples to pull customers away. But people kept walking past him and entering our store *instead*. He watched, arms folded, as a whole family chose us over his free cookies.
instead:1.cnHint: 林在对街摆摊发免费试吃，顾客却____走进了我们的店。
instead:1.hook: Lin picked up his cookie tray and began slowly crossing the road.
instead:1.line: They walked right past me and chose your store *instead*.

performance:1.en: A street musician set up just outside the entrance. His *performance* was so lively that a crowd gathered on the pavement, blocking the store door completely. The Manager watched through the glass, torn between joy at the crowd and panic that no one could actually get inside.
performance:1.cnHint: 一位街头音乐人在门口____太精彩，把入口堵得水泄不通。
performance:1.hook: The musician winked at the Manager and played even louder.
performance:1.line: My *performance* always draws a crowd — you should thank me.

percent:1.en: The Manager had taped a sign to the door: FIFTY *PERCENT* OFF ALL DRINKS. A long queue formed quickly on the pavement. But he had forgotten to check the stock first. By the time I counted the bottles inside, I felt a cold knot in my stomach.
percent:1.cnHint: 店长在门口贴出饮料____折的海报，队伍排得很长，但库存……
percent:1.hook: The first customer in line was already holding out exact change.
percent:1.line: Fifty *percent* off — every drink, right now, no limit!

achieve:1.en: Tang had bet the Manager she could sell thirty bags of chips before noon just by standing outside and smiling at passers-by. No words, just a smile. By eleven-fifty she had sold twenty-nine. She stared at the street, willing someone to walk over. To *achieve* thirty felt huge.
achieve:1.cnHint: 唐打赌只靠微笑就能在中午前卖出三十包薯片，还差最后一包。
achieve:1.hook: A dog walker paused, looked at the chips, then looked at Tang.
achieve:1.line: I will *achieve* thirty bags before that clock strikes noon.

challenge:1.en: Lin walked across the street and stopped in front of our sale sign. He crossed his arms and looked at me. 'I *challenge* you,' he said quietly, 'to match my prices.' He slid a handwritten list across the pavement with his shoe. I picked it up. My hands went cold.
challenge:1.cnHint: 林走过来，把一张价格单推到我脚边，正式____我们。
challenge:1.hook: Every price on his list was lower than ours by exactly one yuan.
challenge:1.line: I *challenge* you to beat these prices this weekend.

power:1.en: At midnight the street lights on our corner flickered and went out. The store stayed bright, but outside it was suddenly very dark. A couple who had been reading our window menu stepped back, unsure. 'We still have *power*,' I called out from the doorway. They looked relieved and stepped inside.
power:1.cnHint: 路灯突然灭了，我在门口告诉驻足的顾客，我们店还有____。
power:1.hook: Behind me, somewhere deep in the store, something beeped twice.

receive:1.en: Saturday morning. A delivery van stops outside the store. The Manager rushes out, clipboard in hand, counting boxes stacked on the pavement. 'Sign here,' the driver says. The Manager checks each label twice. We are about to *receive* forty cases of weekend sale stock, and not a single one matches the order sheet.
receive:1.cnHint: 店长在店门口____了一大批促销货物，却发现数量对不上。
receive:1.hook: One box is ticking softly from inside.
receive:1.line: 'We *receive* forty cases, but the list says thirty-eight.'

encourage:1.en: Lin stands on the pavement handing out small flyers for a rival shop two streets away. She spots me taping our sale poster to the window and grins. 'Nice try,' she calls. But the Manager appears beside me and gives my shoulder a firm pat. 'Let her watch,' he says, trying to *encourage* me to keep going.
encourage:1.cnHint: 店长在门口____我继续贴海报，不要在意竞争对手林。
encourage:1.hook: Lin folds one of our flyers and slips it into her pocket.
encourage:1.line: 'I always *encourage* my team before a big sale day.'

travel:1.en: Old Mr. Chen arrives before sunrise, pulling a small cart loaded with homemade rice balls. He says the same thing every Saturday: the best customers *travel* all the way from the new apartments just to buy from our corner. He sets his cart beside our entrance without asking, arranges the balls neatly, and winks at me.
travel:1.cnHint: 陈大爷说顾客们会专程____到我们这个街角来买东西。
travel:1.hook: This Saturday, his cart carries something wrapped in dark cloth.
travel:1.line: 'People *travel* far for good food — remember that, young clerk.'

strong:1.en: The weekend wind picks up just as Tang and I finish hanging a long banner across the store front. The banner snaps hard in the gust. Tang tests the rope with both hands and nods. 'The knot is *strong*,' she says. She is right — the banner holds while every other shop's sign along the street tears loose.
strong:1.cnHint: 唐检查了绳结，确认它____，足以撑过大风。
strong:1.hook: Then one corner nail begins to pull slowly from the wall.
strong:1.line: 'Don't worry — this knot is *strong* enough for any storm.'

chance:1.en: A woman in a yellow coat stops at our window display, stares at the stacked tins, then walks away. A minute later she is back. The Manager leans over to me and whispers that this is our *chance* to show her the weekend deal before she crosses the street to Lin's shop. I open the door and smile.
chance:1.cnHint: 店长低声提醒我，现在是抓住这位顾客的____。
chance:1.hook: The woman's yellow coat hides a staff badge from Lin's store.
chance:1.line: 'This is our *chance*, so go and greet her warmly.'

solve:1.en: Tang discovers a jammed price-tag printer right when the Saturday rush begins. Customers are already queuing at the door. The Manager paces. I borrow a thick marker from the stationery rack and hand-write every price on plain cards. It takes six minutes to *solve* the problem, and the queue does not complain — much.
solve:1.cnHint: 标价打印机坏了，我用记号笔手写价格卡，____了这个问题。
solve:1.hook: But the Manager notices one card has the wrong price on it.
solve:1.line: 'Good — you *solve* small problems before they grow big.'

quite:1.en: By mid-morning the pavement outside is *quite* crowded. Families with pushchairs, elderly neighbours with bags, and school kids pressing their faces to the glass all squeeze past each other in front of our door. Tang stands just inside, keeping count on a small notebook. She has never seen a Saturday like this in two years of working here.
quite:1.cnHint: 今天上午街边____热闹，唐说这是她两年来没见过的盛况。
quite:1.hook: Tang's notebook count suddenly skips from forty to sixty-three.
quite:1.line: 'It is *quite* busy — stay near the door and guide them in.'

technology:1.en: A teenager outside is using his phone to scan the QR code on our sale poster. He taps the screen, frowns, taps again. 'Your link is broken,' he tells me. I had no idea the Manager had added any *technology* to the promotion at all. I call inside for help, and Tang comes out holding a printed sheet with the correct code.
technology:1.cnHint: 店长在海报上加入了____功能，但二维码链接出了问题。
technology:1.hook: Tang's sheet shows a link to a page none of us have seen.
technology:1.line: 'New *technology* is great — when someone remembers to test it.'

key:1.en: Saturday morning. A sale banner stretches across the store front. I arrive early, but the metal door will not open. I check my pockets twice. The *key* the Manager gave me on my first day — gone. I pat my coat, my bag, every pocket. Nothing. Customers are already lining up outside.
key:1.cnHint: 新店员发现打开店门的____不见了，顾客们已经在外面排队。
key:1.hook: Then I notice a small envelope taped to the door.
key:1.line: 'The *key* should be on a red ring — did you check your jacket?'

issue:1.en: The street outside is busy with weekend shoppers. A man in a grey coat stops me as I carry boxes from the delivery van. He holds up a folded paper. 'There is an *issue* with your weekend price list,' he says, pointing at a number. 'This drink is marked twice.' He looks very serious.
issue:1.cnHint: 一位顾客在门口拦住店员，说促销价格表上有一处____。
issue:1.hook: Behind him, a small crowd has already gathered to look.
issue:1.line: 'That *issue* will cost you customers if you do not fix it fast.'

against:1.en: Strong wind sweeps down the street just as I step outside to hang the sale sign. I lean the ladder *against* the wall and climb up slowly. The sign flaps and pulls like a kite. Tang stands at the bottom, holding the ladder with both hands, shouting something I cannot hear.
against:1.cnHint: 店员爬梯子挂促销横幅，把梯子____着墙壁，风刮得很猛。
against:1.hook: At that moment, the ladder begins to slide.
against:1.line: 'Keep the ladder flat *against* the wall or it will slip!'

matter:1.en: A small girl tugs my sleeve near the entrance. She holds a coin purse and stares at the price tag on a snack box with a worried face. 'Does the discount *matter* for this one too?' she asks. Her older brother stands behind her, counting coins in his palm very carefully.
matter:1.cnHint: 一个小女孩在店门口问店员，打折优惠对她选的零食是否也____。
matter:1.hook: The brother's coin count comes up exactly one coin short.
matter:1.line: 'It *matters* a lot — save five yuan and you can grab one more.'

raise:1.en: The Manager stands on the pavement, studying the handwritten price board I put up earlier. He tilts his head. 'You need to *raise* the bottom line by two centimetres,' he says, tapping the board. 'People walking past cannot read it.' He hands me the marker and watches with his arms crossed.
raise:1.cnHint: 店长让店员把门口价格牌上的字____高两厘米，方便路人看清。
raise:1.hook: Lin walks by, glances at the board, and says nothing at all.
raise:1.line: '*Raise* that last line — short people will miss the best deal.'

option:1.en: A woman with two heavy bags stops outside and stares at our weekend bundle display. 'Is there any other *option* besides the large pack?' she asks me. 'I live alone. The large size is too much.' She looks tired. I think fast, then point to a sign she has clearly missed.
option:1.cnHint: 一位独居的顾客问店员，大包装之外是否还有别的____。
option:1.hook: The sign she missed changes everything about her evening plans.
option:1.line: 'Your best *option* is the small bundle — same price, less waste.'

society:1.en: Outside, a student group sets up a small stand near our entrance. They wear matching yellow vests. Their banner reads: 'Campus Reading *Society* — Free Book Swap.' They ask if they can place a box of books beside our door. The Manager watches from inside, arms folded, expression unreadable.
society:1.cnHint: 一个校园阅读____的同学们在店门口摆摊换书，请求把书箱放在门边。
society:1.hook: The Manager picks up one of the books and turns it over slowly.
society:1.line: 'Our *society* just needs one small corner — we will be very tidy.'

whole:1.en: I step outside to collect the sandwich board after the morning rush. The street is quieter now. I look back at the store — the bright lights, the neat shelves visible through the glass, the little queue at the counter — and realise the *whole* block smells of fresh coffee from our machine.
whole:1.cnHint: 早高峰结束后，店员站在门口回望整间店，发现____条街都飘着咖啡香。
whole:1.hook: A stranger pauses, sniffs the air, and walks straight in.
whole:1.line: 'The *whole* street can smell that coffee — you will be busy again soon.'

nearly:1.en: The Manager asked me to set up the weekend sale display outside before sunrise. I carried box after box of snacks and drinks onto the pavement. By the time I finished, I had *nearly* dropped a whole tray of juice bottles — my hands were shaking from the cold. Tang caught the tray just in time and gave me a tired thumbs-up.
nearly:1.cnHint: 店长让我在日出前把促销展示台搬到店外，我____把一托盘果汁摔在地上。
nearly:1.hook: But why was Tang already outside at four in the morning?
nearly:1.line: 'You *nearly* lost all twelve bottles — good thing I was here.'

wrong:1.en: Lin stood outside our store, staring at the sale signs I had just put up. Something about Lin's face told me a *wrong* price had slipped through. I checked the tag on the sparkling water — it said two yuan instead of twelve. Lin smiled, said nothing, and walked away. I fixed it fast, my ears turning red.
wrong:1.cnHint: 林盯着我贴的促销价签，我意识到上面有一个____的数字。
wrong:1.hook: Had Lin already photographed the tag?
wrong:1.line: 'That price is *wrong* — you might want to fix it quickly.'

variety:1.en: For the weekend sale the Manager told me to group the snacks by type outside the entrance. I was surprised by the *variety* of things we sold — dried fruit, rice crackers, seaweed chips, and even small jars of spicy sauce. A kid stopped, eyes wide, and pointed at nearly everything. Her grandmother just sighed and opened her purse.
variety:1.cnHint: 周末大促时，我把零食分类摆出来，才发现店里售卖的东西____真丰富。
variety:1.hook: The grandmother whispered something to the kid that made them both laugh.
variety:1.line: 'Look at this *variety* — I do not know where to start!'

clear:1.en: I wrote the sale prices on a small whiteboard and set it on the pavement. Tang walked past, squinted, and shook his head. My handwriting was too small. I rubbed it all out and wrote again, big and bold this time. Now it was *clear* enough to read from across the street. An old man nodded at it approvingly and walked straight in.
clear:1.cnHint: 我在小白板上写了促销价，但字太小，重新写了一遍，终于____可以让对面的人看到了。
clear:1.hook: The old man came out holding something we did not even know was on sale.
clear:1.line: 'Much better — now it is *clear* for everyone passing by.'

gain:1.en: By eight in the morning a short queue had formed outside. I watched people fill their baskets quickly, and I started to understand what the weekend sale was really about. Every small purchase was a *gain* for the store, yes, but the real reward was the warm feeling of neighbours choosing us over the bigger shop down the road. Lin peered over from across the street.
gain:1.cnHint: 周末早上门外排起了队，我意识到每一笔小销售都是店里的一份____。
gain:1.hook: Lin was writing something in a small notebook.
gain:1.line: 'Every loyal customer is a *gain* we should never take for granted.'

maybe:1.en: A tall woman in a rain jacket stopped at our outdoor display and picked up a bag of rice crackers, then put it back, then picked it up again. She looked at me. I shrugged. She said she was trying to eat less salt. I told her, honestly, that those crackers were *maybe* the lightest option we had outside. She bought two bags.
maybe:1.cnHint: 一位顾客拿起又放下米饼好几次，我告诉她这____是我们外摆里最淡口的选择。
maybe:1.hook: She asked if we carried anything with no salt at all.
maybe:1.line: 'This is *maybe* the best deal I have seen all weekend.'

huge:1.en: The Manager dragged a *huge* red banner out from the back room and asked Tang and me to hang it above the entrance. It was twice as wide as the doorway. Tang stood on a step stool; I held the other end on my toes. A passing cyclist slowed down to watch, almost rode into a bin, and then stopped to read the banner properly.
huge:1.cnHint: 店长拿出一条____的红色横幅，让我和唐帮忙挂在门口上方。
huge:1.hook: The cyclist locked their bike and walked inside without a word.
huge:1.line: 'That is a *huge* banner — the whole street can see it now.'

diet:1.en: A regular customer — a quiet man who always bought plain yoghurt — stood outside studying the sale table with a worried expression. He picked up a bag of chocolate biscuits, checked the back, and set it down. He told me he was on a strict *diet* and could not afford any surprises. I pointed him toward the unsweetened drinks shelf inside. He looked grateful.
diet:1.cnHint: 一位常客站在促销台前，告诉我他在严格控制____，不能乱买零食。
diet:1.hook: He paused at the door and turned back to look at the biscuits one more time.
diet:1.line: 'I am on a *diet*, so I have to be careful about everything I pick up.'

animal:1.en: A boy pressed his face against the glass door, staring at the small shelf of toy figures near the counter. 'Which one is your favourite *animal*?' I asked, turning the tiger toward him. His eyes went wide. He pointed at the shark instead, then at his pocket, then looked up at me hopefully.
animal:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩盯着货架上的玩具，用手指了指鲨鱼，又指了指自己的口袋，眼神充满期待，好像在说他的零花钱可能不太够买____。
animal:1.hook: He reached into his pocket and pulled out something far more interesting than coins.
animal:1.line: 'That *animal* is the best one on the whole shelf,' he said firmly.

goal:1.en: Tang swept the area outside the door just before midnight, humming to himself. 'You seem happy,' I said through the open door. 'My *goal* this week is to keep the front step cleaner than the coffee shop next door,' he said, nodding toward the rival store across the street. He was winning, apparently.
goal:1.cnHint: 阿糖在午夜前打扫门口，他告诉我他这周的____是把台阶扫得比对面咖啡店更干净。
goal:1.hook: The coffee shop door swung open, and someone stepped out with a mop.
goal:1.line: 'My *goal* is simple: the cleanest step on this street,' Tang said.

adult:1.en: A teenager counted coins on the counter for the third time, one short for a hot drink. Behind her, a quiet man in a coat waited without a word, then slid an extra coin forward. 'An *adult* thing to do,' I thought, but said nothing. She left warm. He just nodded and bought his water.
adult:1.cnHint: 一个硬币不够的少年，被身后一个陌生____默默补上了差额，然后那人买了瓶水就走了。
adult:1.hook: I saw the same coat again the next night, but the face below it was different.
adult:1.line: 'Acting like an *adult* means you help without making a big deal,' he said quietly.

poor:1.en: Lin from the rival coffee shop came in at two in the morning looking tired. 'Long night?' I asked. '*Poor* planning on my part,' she said, dropping onto the stool by the window. 'I ordered three times the cups we needed and now I have to count them all.' She bought a hot drink and stayed a while.
poor:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林深夜走进来，抱怨自己____的计划导致她要数三倍数量的杯子。
poor:1.hook: She left a sticky note on the window that I did not find until morning.
poor:1.line: '*Poor* planning is my real talent,' Lin said, and actually laughed.

price:1.en: The Manager taped a new sign to the door before leaving for the evening: WEEKEND SALE — ALL DRINKS HALF *PRICE*. I read it four times. Then I looked at our stock. Then I looked at the sign again. By midnight the shelf was nearly empty, and a small crowd was still growing outside the glass.
price:1.cnHint: 店长贴出了周末半____的告示，到午夜货架已经快空了，门外还有人在排队。
price:1.hook: Someone at the back of the crowd was writing something down in a notebook.
price:1.line: 'Half *price* means we work twice as hard tonight,' I told myself.

type:1.en: Tang was sorting the snack display when a regular came in and stared for a long time. 'I want the salty *type*,' the man said at last, waving at the whole row. Tang and I looked at each other. We spent ten minutes holding up bags one by one until the man nodded. He seemed very satisfied.
type:1.cnHint: 一位常客盯着零食架想了很久，只说想要咸____的那种，我和阿糖一袋一袋举给他看。
type:1.hook: He came back twenty minutes later and asked for the sweet type.
type:1.line: 'I only like this *type*,' the man said, hugging the bag to his chest.

sense:1.en: Just after three in the morning a woman stood outside the door for a full minute before coming in. She walked the aisles slowly, picking nothing up. 'Can I help you?' I asked. She smiled. 'I just needed the *sense* that somewhere was still open,' she said. She bought a small juice and left looking lighter.
sense:1.cnHint: 一位女士在凌晨三点走进来，说她只是需要一种____——知道某个地方还开着。
sense:1.hook: She left her umbrella behind, though the sky outside was perfectly clear.
sense:1.line: 'Sometimes you just need the *sense* that the world is still awake,' she said.

rate:1.en: Lin leaned on the counter at dawn, comparing notes on foot traffic. 'Your sale *rate* last night was incredible,' she said, sounding slightly impressed and slightly annoyed. 'Half-price drinks,' I said. She was quiet for a moment. Then: 'I might hate you a little.' She bought two drinks and left smiling anyway.
rate:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在黎明时分过来，提到我们昨晚的销售____很惊人，然后说她可能有点恨我们。
rate:1.hook: She came back an hour later with a sign of her own and taped it to her window.
rate:1.line: 'That sale *rate* should be illegal,' Lin said, but she was smiling.

within:1.en: The Manager taped a bright sign to our door: everything on the front shelf was on sale. 'All items must be sold *within* two hours,' he told me, tapping his watch. By the time I looked up, a woman in a yellow coat had already cleared half the shelf without a word.
within:1.cnHint: 店长规定促销商品必须在两小时____售完，一位黄衣女士动作极快。
within:1.hook: She came back an hour later, and she was not alone.
within:1.line: 'All discounts must be used *within* today, so hurry!' said the Manager.

either:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street leaned in our doorway during the sale rush. 'Your prices are lower, but your coffee isn't good,' he said with a shrug. I didn't argue. He didn't leave, *either*. He just stood there, slowly eating one of our discounted meat buns.
either:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林虽然嘴上挑剔，却____没有离开，站着吃起了打折肉包。
either:1.hook: He left a small note on the counter before he finally walked out.
either:1.line: 'I do not like your layout, and I do not trust your coffee, *either*,' said Lin.

various:1.en: For the weekend sale, the Manager had stacked *various* snacks near the door — chips, dried fruit, little cakes, and things I couldn't name. Each bag had a cheerful red tag. A boy stopped in front of the display for a very long time, clearly doing very serious math in his head.
various:1.cnHint: 促销期间店门口摆满了____各式各样的零食，一个小男孩站在那里默默地计算着。
various:1.hook: He pulled out a tiny notebook before choosing anything.
various:1.line: 'I put out *various* snacks so every kind of customer finds something,' said the Manager.

main:1.en: Tang pointed at the street outside and said the *main* reason people stopped at our store was the corner position — easy to see, easy to reach. I watched the door all evening and decided she was right. But one old man walked past four times before coming in, as if making up his mind.
main:1.cnHint: 阿糖说地理位置是顾客光顾的____原因，但有位老人在门外来回走了四次。
main:1.hook: When he finally entered, he asked for something we didn't carry.
main:1.line: 'The *main* reason this store works is the corner — people see us first,' said Tang.

employee:1.en: A woman stopped me near the entrance and asked if I was a new *employee*. I said yes, just started this week. She smiled and said she had seen four new clerks in two years. She said it in a kind way, not a worried one. Then she bought a single piece of gum and left.
employee:1.cnHint: 一位女顾客问我是不是新来的____，她说两年内她见过四个新店员了。
employee:1.hook: She turned back at the door and added one last quiet remark.
employee:1.line: 'So you are the new *employee*? The Manager always picks the night shift ones carefully,' she said.

class:1.en: Three students spilled in after midnight, still in the middle of a loud debate. One of them slapped the counter and said their study *class* had just ended and they needed sugar immediately. I sold them three of everything sweet we had. They left still arguing, but happier.
class:1.cnHint: 三个学生深夜冲进来，说他们的补习____刚结束，急需补充糖分。
class:1.hook: One of them left a folded piece of paper near the register.
class:1.line: 'Our exam prep *class* just ended — we survived, so we deserve snacks,' said one student.

behavior:1.en: Tang quietly pulled me aside after a customer left the store without paying for a small drink. 'Watch the door,' she said. 'It's not the first time.' She wasn't angry — just calm, like she had seen every kind of *behavior* in this store and none of it surprised her anymore.
behavior:1.cnHint: 一位顾客没付钱就走了，阿糖平静地说她见过各种各样的____，早已不觉得奇怪。
behavior:1.hook: The same customer returned twenty minutes later with exact change.
behavior:1.line: 'In this store you see every kind of *behavior* — the night shift teaches you fast,' said Tang.

disease:1.en: An older man bought three bottles of herbal drink and told me his doctor said stress was a modern *disease* worse than a cold. He looked very unbothered for someone worried about stress. He tucked the bottles into a tote bag, patted the counter twice, and walked into the dark street.
disease:1.cnHint: 一位老先生说医生告诉他压力是一种现代____，但他本人看起来十分淡定。
disease:1.hook: The label on one of his bottles was handwritten, not printed.
disease:1.line: 'My doctor says stress is a *disease*, so I buy these every Friday without fail,' the old man said.

action:1.en: The Manager taped a big red sign to the door before sunrise. 'Weekend sale starts now,' he said, clapping his hands. 'We need *action*, not standing around.' I grabbed a mop, Tang grabbed a price gun, and somehow the tiny store felt like the centre of the whole street.
action:1.cnHint: 店长要求大家赶紧____起来，备战周末促销。
action:1.hook: Then a figure across the street began writing something on a chalkboard.
action:1.line: 'We need *action*, not standing around — move those displays outside now!'

program:1.en: Tang had written a whole *program* for the weekend sale on the back of a receipt: greet customers, push the two-for-one drinks, offer free bags. It was only eight steps, but she spoke about it like a general reading a battle plan. I memorised every line.
program:1.cnHint: 阿糖制定了一份详细的促销____，每一步都清清楚楚。
program:1.hook: Step seven had a small star next to it, but Tang would not explain why.
program:1.line: 'Follow the *program* exactly and we will be fine — trust me on step seven.'

situation:1.en: By nine in the morning the pavement outside was crowded with shoppers and the queue reached the door. I looked at Tang, unsure what to do. She took one glance at the *situation* and opened the second register without a word. I felt grateful and slightly embarrassed.
situation:1.cnHint: 早上九点，门口排起了长队，阿糖迅速判断了____并打开了第二台收银机。
situation:1.hook: One customer at the back of the queue kept checking the store across the street.
situation:1.line: 'The *situation* is under control — just keep smiling and scan faster.'

order:1.en: A man in a raincoat handed me a handwritten list: six rice balls, four teas, two hot soups. 'It is a standing *order* every Saturday,' Tang whispered. 'He never changes it.' I packed everything in two minutes flat and felt oddly proud of my speed.
order:1.cnHint: 一位穿雨衣的顾客每周六都有固定____，内容一成不变。
order:1.hook: This time he lingered by the door, glancing at a note in his hand.
order:1.line: 'Same *order* as last week, please — you will get used to me soon enough.'

event:1.en: The Manager had printed flyers calling the weekend sale a 'community *event*.' That felt grand for a store the size of a parking space, but people did come — neighbours with tote bags, students with coins, an old man who just wanted somewhere warm to stand for a while.
event:1.cnHint: 店长把周末促销称为一场社区____，吸引了各种各样的街坊邻居。
event:1.hook: The old man in the corner had not bought anything yet, but he kept smiling at the door.
event:1.line: 'Welcome to our little *event* — there is a free sample by the register.'

account:1.en: Lin from the store across the street strolled in at noon, phone raised, filming everything. 'Research,' she said sweetly. Tang gave a slow blink. Later the Manager said Lin had posted an *account* of our sale online, calling our prices 'surprisingly reasonable.' Tang printed it and stuck it on the fridge.
account:1.cnHint: 对面店的隔壁咖啡店的林在网上发布了一篇对我们促销活动的____，措辞出人意料地友好。
account:1.hook: But Lin had circled something in the post with a red pen before she left.
account:1.line: 'I posted a fair *account* — your dumplings really are better than I expected.'

deal:1.en: A student emptied her pockets on the counter: coins, a crumpled bill, a bus pass. She needed one more yuan for the meal set. I paused, then quietly took one yuan from the small tips jar beside the register. 'That is a *deal*,' I said. She beamed so wide I forgot I was tired.
deal:1.cnHint: 一个学生差一元钱，我悄悄补上，达成了这笔____。
deal:1.hook: She came back twenty minutes later and left something small on the counter without a word.
deal:1.line: 'That is a *deal* — and please come back when you have more coins next time.'

degree:1.en: The soup machine broke at two in the afternoon and the temperature inside the cups dropped to a useless *degree*. The Manager poked it twice and sighed. Tang found a power switch behind a shelf and the machine hummed back to life. The Manager stared at the shelf for a long moment.
degree:1.cnHint: 汤机坏了，温度降到了没用的____，阿糖找到了隐藏的开关解决了问题。
degree:1.hook: The Manager quietly moved three boxes to check what else might be hiding behind that shelf.
degree:1.line: 'The temperature had dropped to a *degree* where nobody would buy it — good catch, Tang.'

worker:1.en: Saturday morning, a road crew blocked half the street outside the store. One *worker* in an orange vest kept waving cars away from a broken pipe. I watched from behind the glass door, holding a mop I did not need, glad the noise stayed outside.
worker:1.cnHint: 一名施工____挡在店门口，让早班变得格外热闹。
worker:1.hook: Then he stepped inside, mud on his boots and urgency in his eyes.
worker:1.line: 'Excuse me — I'm a *worker* out there, can I use your phone?'

control:1.en: A small dog tied to the bike rack outside went wild every time someone walked past. Its owner, an older man buying instant noodles, rushed out three times to calm it. By the third trip I could see he was losing *control* of both the dog and his temper.
control:1.cnHint: 门外那条小狗完全不受____，主人跑进跑出好几回。
control:1.hook: On the fourth bark, something on the noodle shelf came crashing down.
control:1.line: 'I'm sorry — I just can't *control* him when he smells food.'

product:1.en: A woman set up a small folding table right outside our door and began showing neighbours a bottle of thick green liquid. She called it a miracle *product* that could clean anything. The Manager watched through the window, arms crossed, saying nothing — which was somehow worse than saying something.
product:1.cnHint: 一位女士在门口推销一款神奇____，把店长气得沉默不语。
product:1.hook: Then she held the bottle up next to our store sign and smiled at a passing camera.
product:1.line: 'This *product* will outsell everything in that store, I promise you.'

practice:1.en: Every Sunday a teenager sat on the low wall across from us and played a small keyboard through a tiny speaker. It was his outdoor *practice* spot, he said, because his mum banned noise at home after nine. The notes floated in each time someone opened our door.
practice:1.cnHint: 一个少年把我们店门口当作他的户外____场地，每周都来报到。
practice:1.hook: Tonight he stopped mid-song and stared at something above the store roof.
practice:1.line: 'I come here to *practice* because nobody shouts at me outside.'

environment:1.en: A city inspector walked slowly past the store, taking notes on a clipboard. She paused to look at our bin area, then at the cracked pavement, then at the bright lights above the door. 'The *environment* here affects everyone on the street,' she said, half to me and half to herself.
environment:1.cnHint: 一位检查员在门外评估街道____，顺带打量了我们的店面。
environment:1.hook: She circled something on her clipboard twice before walking away.
environment:1.line: 'A clean *environment* outside your store matters more than you think.'

system:1.en: Just before midnight the traffic lights at our corner went dark. No green, no red — nothing. Drivers crept forward, unsure who should go. A delivery rider told me the whole signal *system* in this block had tripped. I stood in the doorway watching the polite, slow chaos unfold.
system:1.cnHint: 路口的红绿灯____突然失灵，深夜的街角乱成一锅粥。
system:1.hook: Then one very confident car simply did not slow down at all.
system:1.line: 'The whole light *system* is down — I've already called it in.'

natural:1.en: After a short rain the street smelled like wet concrete and something green from the small trees by the kerb. A regular customer stopped under our awning, closed his eyes, and breathed in slowly. 'That smell is so *natural*,' he said, looking almost happy for the first time I had seen.
natural:1.cnHint: 一场小雨后，一位常客在门口深吸一口____的气息，神情放松。
natural:1.hook: Then he opened his eyes and handed me a very damp shopping list.
natural:1.line: 'Nothing beats that *natural* smell after rain, don't you think?'

free:1.en: A woman was handing out small paper fans on the pavement, each printed with a cartoon cat. 'Completely *free*,' she told everyone who passed, smiling wide. Most people took one without stopping. I got one too, through the door, and used it to fan the warm air near the register all night.
free:1.cnHint: 一位女士在门外派发____的纸扇，连我也收到了一把。
free:1.hook: By midnight I noticed every fan had a tiny phone number printed on the back.
free:1.line: 'Take one — it's totally *free*, no catch at all!'

mind:1.en: The Saturday sale turned the quiet street outside into a small river of people. I stepped out to fix a fallen sign, and the noise hit me at once. A woman stopped, closed her eyes, and took a slow breath. 'I have to *mind* my thoughts,' she said, 'or the crowd pulls them away.' She bought nothing, just smiled and walked on.
mind:1.cnHint: 促销日街上人群嘈杂，一位女士驻足，说她需要____自己的思绪，然后微笑离去。
mind:1.hook: She came back an hour later, bought one small notebook, and said nothing.
mind:1.line: 'I have to *mind* my thoughts, or the crowd pulls them away.'

rise:1.en: By ten in the morning the number of people on the street corner had seen a sharp *rise*. I watched from the doorway as the crowd pushed past our small A-board sign. Tang appeared beside me, arms full of extra stock. 'Every big sale weekend is the same,' she said. 'Enjoy the calm while it lasts.'
rise:1.cnHint: 周末促销，街角人流量出现明显____，同事唐提醒我趁早享受片刻安静。
rise:1.hook: Then a man with a very large cart appeared around the corner, heading straight for us.
rise:1.line: 'Every big sale weekend sees a *rise* like this — enjoy the calm while it lasts.'

prove:1.en: Lin from the shop across the road set up a bright outdoor display right opposite ours. The Manager watched through the window, arms folded. 'They want to *prove* they have better prices,' he said quietly. I stacked our own sale items a little straighter and hoped he was wrong. The street hummed around us.
prove:1.cnHint: 对面的林摆出促销展示，店长说对方想____自己价格更低，我默默把货物摆得更整齐。
