prove:1.hook: A customer stood between both displays for a long moment, then turned toward our door.
prove:1.line: 'They just want to *prove* their prices are better — we'll show them otherwise.'

associate:1.en: Outside, a group of students was debating which snacks to buy. One of them pointed at our window and said something to the others. Tang nudged me. 'They *associate* this store with late-night study food,' she said. 'That's the best kind of regular customer.' The group filed in noisily, and the small store felt suddenly full of life.
associate:1.cnHint: 一群学生在外面讨论，同事唐说他们把这家店和深夜学习零食____在一起，这是最好的回头客。
associate:1.hook: One of them asked, very seriously, if we sold anything that would help them stay awake until dawn.
associate:1.line: 'They *associate* this store with late-night study food — best kind of regular.'

message:1.en: A cyclist stopped hard outside, nearly knocking over our outdoor basket of discounted goods. He checked his phone, let out a long breath, and laughed. 'Wrong street,' he called to me. 'I missed a *message* from my friend. He moved the meeting point.' He bought a cold drink, straightened our basket with one hand, and pedalled away fast.
message:1.cnHint: 一位骑车人急停在门外，说他漏看了朋友发的____，跑错了地方，买了饮料后迅速离开。
message:1.hook: His friend appeared five minutes later, looking just as lost and out of breath.
message:1.line: 'I missed a *message* from my friend — wrong street entirely!'

development:1.en: The Manager unfolded a printed map and spread it on the outdoor table. He traced a line with his finger. 'This whole area is part of a new *development* plan,' he said. 'More apartments, more people, more late-night customers for us.' I looked at the quiet street corner we were standing on and tried to picture it busy and bright.
development:1.cnHint: 店长展开地图，说这一带纳入了新的____计划，将来会有更多公寓和夜间顾客。
development:1.hook: A construction worker walked past just then and gave the map a long, knowing look.
development:1.line: 'This block is part of the new *development* plan — more customers for us soon.'

later:1.en: An old man sat on the low wall outside, resting his feet. He had bought a coffee from us and was in no hurry at all. 'I will pay the rest *later*,' he told me, patting his empty pocket with a kind smile. I was about to speak when Tang appeared, waved a hand, and said it was already covered. The old man nodded slowly, as if he had expected nothing less.
later:1.cnHint: 一位老人在门外休息，说剩下的钱____再付，同事唐出现后直接说已经结清了。
later:1.hook: Tang whispered to me that the old man had once helped the Manager on a very bad night.
later:1.line: 'I will pay the rest *later* — my pocket is a little light today, I am afraid.'

maintain:1.en: Lin had borrowed our outdoor extension lead without asking, and the Manager noticed at once. He walked over, very politely, and unplugged it. 'We *maintain* this equipment ourselves,' he said, keeping his voice even and his face calm. Lin looked surprised, then nodded slowly. Back inside, Tang gave the Manager a quiet thumbs-up behind the counter.
maintain:1.cnHint: 林未经许可借用了店里的设备，店长平静地取回并说明他们自己____这些设备，同事唐悄悄竖起大拇指。
maintain:1.hook: Lin smiled on the way out and said they would talk again very soon.
maintain:1.line: 'We *maintain* this equipment ourselves — please ask next time, and we will help.'

traditional:1.en: The weekly street market set up early outside our store. Vendors spread out red cloth and paper lanterns in the *traditional* style, just as they had every Saturday for thirty years. The Manager stood at the door, watching with a quiet smile, arms crossed.
traditional:1.cnHint: 店长站在门口，看着门外按____ 方式布置的集市，若有所思。
traditional:1.hook: Then he muttered something about one stall that should not be there.
traditional:1.line: This *traditional* setup is nice, but that new vendor worries me.

expert:1.en: A small crowd gathered around a man fixing bicycle wheels on the pavement just outside. His hands moved without hesitation — tightening, testing, adjusting. Tang came out to throw away a bag and stopped to watch. 'He works like an *expert*,' Tang said quietly, clearly impressed.
expert:1.cnHint: 唐在门外看到一个修车人，觉得他手艺____ 。
expert:1.hook: Nobody knew the man had been watching our store window all morning.
expert:1.line: That guy is a real *expert* — he fixed it in two minutes.

member:1.en: Lin was arguing with someone on the pavement near the entrance. The other person pointed at a small card and kept saying he was a *member* of the weekend market committee, so our store had no right to put display boxes on the footpath. Lin folded her arms and said nothing.
member:1.cnHint: 林与一名自称市集委员会____的人，在门口发生了争执。
member:1.hook: The card, I noticed from inside, had yesterday's date crossed out.
member:1.line: I am a *member* of the committee, so please move those boxes now.

heart:1.en: Just before noon, an old woman paused outside and looked at the sale signs in our window. She pressed one hand to her chest and breathed slowly. The *heart* of the whole street festival, she told a child beside her, had always been this little corner store.
heart:1.cnHint: 一位老奶奶在橱窗前停步，说这家小店是整条街节日气氛的____。
heart:1.hook: Then she added that something important had gone missing from it.
heart:1.line: This store is the *heart* of our street, and I miss what it was.

contribute:2.en: A handwritten note sat taped to the donation jar by the door. It read: 'Weekend sale — every purchase will *contribute* to new books for the neighbourhood kids.' The Manager had placed it there himself before the rush. I read it twice, then straightened it so every customer could see.
contribute:2.cnHint: 店长在捐款罐上贴了一张字条，说明这次促销活动将____于附近孩子的图书购买。
contribute:2.hook: But the jar had been opened — and something was missing.
contribute:2.line: 'Every small coin can *contribute* to a child's future,' the Manager said quietly.

share:2.en: During the morning rush, Tang slid a warm meat bun across the counter to me without a word. 'Weekend sale means no break,' she said. 'So we *share* the last bun.' It was a small thing, but after three hours on my feet, that single bun felt like the best meal I had ever had.
share:2.cnHint: 大促期间，同事阿糖把最后一个肉包和我____，让漫长的早班轻松了一点。
share:2.hook: Tang then pulled out a second bag — and smiled strangely.
share:2.line: 'Here, take your *share* before the next wave of customers hits,' Tang said.

decade:2.en: While restocking the back shelf, I found a dusty logbook dated ten years ago. The Manager had kept records every single day for a *decade* — each page filled with neat handwriting, counting every carton of milk and every packet of instant noodles. I set it down carefully, almost afraid to breathe.
decade:2.cnHint: 在货架背后，我发现了一本店长坚持写了____的旧账本。
decade:2.hook: The last entry stopped mid-sentence, ink still slightly smeared.
decade:2.line: 'I have kept this store running for a *decade*,' the Manager said, not looking up.

kind:2.en: A small girl tugged my sleeve and pointed at the snack wall. 'Which *kind* is not too spicy?' she asked in a tiny voice. I crouched down and studied every packet with her as if it were the most important task in the world. We chose a lightly salted one together. She beamed.
kind:2.cnHint: 一个小女孩向我询问哪____零食不辣，我们一起认真挑选。
kind:2.hook: She paid with coins — far too many for one small packet.
kind:2.line: 'What *kind* of chips do you think my grandma would like?' she asked shyly.

across:2.en: Just past midnight, I noticed a light on in the small repair shop *across* the narrow street. An old man sat alone at his workbench, bent over something tiny. He looked up, caught my eye through the glass, and gave a slow nod. I waved back without thinking.
across:2.cnHint: 深夜，我注意到街道____的修理店里还亮着灯，有个老人独自工作。
across:2.hook: The next morning, a small parcel sat on our doorstep — unwrapped.
across:2.line: 'The shop *across* the street always sends someone over before a big sale,' Tang said.

factor:2.en: Lin came in just before the afternoon rush and leaned on the counter. 'You know the biggest *factor* in weekend sales?' she said, eyes scanning our neat display. 'Speed at the till.' She tapped her watch, bought a single energy drink, and left without another word. I stared at the till for a long moment.
factor:2.cnHint: 对手隔壁咖啡店的林来店里，提示我周末促销业绩的关键____是收银速度。
factor:2.hook: She had left a small sticky note under the energy drink can.
factor:2.line: 'Speed is the key *factor* today — do not slow down,' Lin said with a smirk.

condition:2.en: The Manager called me to the back room and pointed at the old drinks fridge. 'Check its *condition* before the rush starts,' he said. 'Last weekend it died at noon and we lost half our cold stock.' The fan was making a thin, unhappy sound. I found the instruction sheet and got to work.
condition:2.cnHint: 店长叫我检查旧冰柜的____，以免大促期间再次出故障。
condition:2.hook: The instruction sheet described a fault that matched exactly what I was hearing.
condition:2.line: 'If the *condition* of that fridge is bad, we call the repair man now,' the Manager said firmly.

effort:2.en: By nine in the evening my feet were screaming, but the queue still stretched to the door. Tang caught me slowing down and quietly took over the heavier bags without a word. Later she said, 'Your *effort* tonight kept the line moving.' It was six words, but I felt them all the way home.
effort:2.cnHint: 漫长的夜班结束后，阿糖肯定了我整晚付出的____。
effort:2.hook: She had also quietly written my name in the logbook — under 'best shift'.
effort:2.line: 'I saw your *effort* all night — the Manager saw it too,' Tang said softly.

compare:2.en: The Manager pinned a hand-written sign above the drinks fridge: WEEKEND SPECIAL — *compare* our prices before you leave! I read it three times, feeling oddly proud, as though I had written it myself. Tang noticed and laughed. Just then a quiet woman in a yellow coat studied the sign for a long moment, then pulled out a small notebook and began writing.
compare:2.cnHint: 店长在冰柜上贴了一张特价告示，让顾客____一下价格，一位穿黄色外套的女士看完后默默掏出笔记本。
compare:2.hook: She had filled three pages before she even picked up a single item.
compare:2.line: '*Compare* our prices with any other store — I promise you will stay.'

past:2.en: I found an old logbook under the counter, its pages soft with age. Every night clerk before me had left a short note — spilled coffee, a lost umbrella, one line about a fox outside the door. The *past* of this small store was warmer than I had expected. Tang saw me reading and smiled quietly. One name appeared on nearly every page: a customer called simply 'the Professor.'
past:2.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现了一本旧记录本，翻阅这家小店的____，发现一个叫"教授"的常客几乎每页都有提及。
past:2.hook: Nobody had seen the Professor in over a year.
past:2.line: 'The *past* of this store belongs to everyone who ever stood behind that counter.'

suffer:2.en: The weekend sale brought twice the usual crowd. By midnight the shelf labels were crooked, the floor was sticky, and my feet ached. Tang caught me wincing. 'New shoes?' they asked. I nodded. 'We all *suffer* the first weekend,' Tang said, handing me a small cushioned mat from behind the counter. A tall man near the door was watching us with a faint, knowing smile.
suffer:2.cnHint: 周末大促人潮汹涌，我的新鞋让我____不已，阿糖递来一块软垫，门口一位高个子男人若有所思地看着我们。
suffer:2.hook: He looked like someone who had once stood exactly where I was standing.
suffer:2.line: 'You will *suffer* in new shoes — everyone does on sale weekend.'

almost:2.en: I was restocking the top shelf when a small tin slipped from my hand and fell behind the fridge. I reached in and pulled out the tin — and *almost* dropped it again when I saw what was taped to its bottom: a folded note with a name and a phone number written in careful, old-fashioned letters. Tang glanced over, eyebrows raised. Neither of us recognised the name.
almost:2.cnHint: 我在冰柜后找回一个小铁罐，看到罐底贴着一张字条时____吓了一跳，阿糖也认不出上面写的名字。
almost:2.hook: The number, Tang said softly, had not worked for at least five years.
almost:2.line: 'I *almost* missed it — it was hidden right at the back.'

especially:2.en: The Manager had decorated the store for the weekend sale — little paper stars on every shelf, a cheerful hand-drawn banner above the door. It looked *especially* bright against the dark street outside. I stood by the window watching people slow down as they passed, drawn in by the light. Tang brought two cups of warm tea. One regular stopped, pressed her face to the glass, and grinned like a child.
especially:2.cnHint: 店长为周末大促装点了小店，橱窗在黑夜中____耀眼，一位常客贴着玻璃往里张望，笑得像个孩子。
especially:2.hook: She came in every night, Tang whispered, but had never once bought anything.
especially:2.line: 'It looks *especially* lovely tonight — better than any other weekend.'

publish:2.en: I noticed a neatly folded newspaper left on the counter beside the card reader. Someone had circled a small article with a red pen. The headline read: LOCAL STORE CLERK TO *PUBLISH* COLLECTION OF NIGHT STORIES. There was no photo, only a name — and when Tang walked over and read it, they went very still. The Manager came out of the back room with a strange expression.
publish:2.cnHint: 柜台上有人留下一份报纸，上面用红笔圈出一篇文章——一位便利店夜班店员即将____一本故事集，阿糖看完后久久没有说话。
publish:2.hook: The name in the article was someone none of us had ever heard of — or so we thought.
publish:2.line: 'They are going to *publish* it next month — the night stories from this very street.'

activity:2.en: The Manager had planned a small in-store *activity* for Saturday night: guess the number of sweets in a jar and win a discount. By two in the morning the jar was surrounded by torn slips of paper. I counted forty-one entries. Tang was adding them up at the counter when a delivery driver leaned in from the doorway, looked at the jar, and quietly wrote a number on a slip without saying a word.
activity:2.cnHint: 店长为周末大促策划了一个猜糖果数量的____，一位送货司机悄悄走进来，默默写下一个数字后转身离去。
activity:2.hook: His number was exactly right — but he never came back to claim the prize.
activity:2.line: 'This little *activity* brings more people in than any sale sign ever did.'

science:2.en: A young man spread his notes across the whole snack counter, textbook open to a chapter on *science* — something about light and waves, I could see the diagrams from where I stood. He ordered a hot drink and did not look up for an hour. Tang refilled his cup without being asked. As he finally packed his bag to leave, he tucked a small folded paper under the empty cup.
science:2.cnHint: 一个年轻人把课本摊开在零食柜台上复习____，阿糖悄悄给他续了杯热饮，他离开时在杯子下压了一张折叠的小纸条。
science:2.hook: The note had only four words on it, and none of them were about science.
science:2.line: '*Science* makes more sense at two in the morning, somehow.'

personal:2.en: A folded note had been left under the counter, addressed to nobody in particular. The Manager picked it up and read it twice, his face going very still. 'This is *personal*,' he said quietly, sliding it into his shirt pocket before Tang or I could see a single word.
personal:2.cnHint: 店长在柜台下发现一张折好的纸条，神情变得凝重，说这是____的事。
personal:2.hook: But his hands would not stop shaking all night.
personal:2.line: 'This is *personal* — please don't ask me about it.'

rather:2.en: The stockroom smelled *rather* odd that morning — not bad exactly, but strange, like old paper and something sweet. Tang sniffed the air and said nothing. I found a cardboard box in the corner, sealed with too much tape. Nobody remembered ordering it, and the delivery note had no sender name.
rather:2.cnHint: 库房里有一股____奇怪的气味，角落里出现了一个没有寄件人信息的箱子。
rather:2.hook: The box was warm to the touch.
rather:2.line: 'It smells *rather* strange in here, don't you think?'

instead:2.en: Lin was supposed to drop off the weekend stock report, but she never came through the front door. *Instead*, a small sealed envelope appeared on the mat, pushed under the gap, with only my name written on it in red pen. No explanation. No knock. Just silence outside.
instead:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林没有按约定送来报告，____在门缝下出现了一封写着我名字的红字信封。
instead:2.hook: I was almost sure I heard footsteps running away.
instead:2.line: 'I did not call you — I left a note *instead*.'

performance:2.en: A regular customer, an older man who always bought warm tea, paused at the door and pinned a small flyer to our notice board. It advertised a street *performance* by a group of students, happening right outside our store at midnight. The Manager stared at the flyer for a long time.
performance:2.cnHint: 一位老顾客在公告栏上贴了一张传单，宣传今晚子夜就在店门外的一场学生____。
performance:2.hook: The Manager quietly turned the store music off.
performance:2.line: 'Their *performance* starts right outside at midnight — come look!'

percent:2.en: Tang pointed at the small screen behind the counter. 'Sales are up forty *percent* from last Saturday,' she said, sounding surprised. She printed the report and circled the number with a red pen, then slipped it under the Manager's office door without knocking. A moment later, the door opened just a crack.
percent:2.cnHint: 阿糖发现本周销售额比上周六上涨了四十____，把报告悄悄塞进了店长办公室门缝。
percent:2.hook: Nobody heard what the Manager said inside.
percent:2.line: 'Sales are up forty *percent* — how is that even possible?'

achieve:2.en: I found a sticky note on the refrigerator door in the staff area. It read: 'Anyone who can *achieve* a full weekend count with zero errors gets Sunday morning off.' No name, no date. Tang said she had never seen it before. The Manager, when I asked, simply smiled and walked away.
achieve:2.cnHint: 冰箱门上有张便利贴，承诺谁能____整个周末零差错盘点就可以休息，但没人知道是谁贴的。
achieve:2.hook: Tang had already started counting before I finished reading.
achieve:2.line: 'If you *achieve* a perfect count, Sunday morning is yours.'

challenge:2.en: Tucked inside the daily delivery box, beneath the bread rolls, was a folded card. Written in neat letters: 'Here is your *challenge* — sell every rice ball before 3 a.m. or buy us breakfast.' Tang flipped it over looking for a name. Only a small smiley face smiled back at us.
challenge:2.cnHint: 面包送货箱底部藏着一张卡片，向我们发出____：在凌晨三点前卖完所有饭团，否则请吃早餐。
challenge:2.hook: There were exactly thirty rice balls left.
challenge:2.line: 'This is your *challenge* — every rice ball gone before three.'

power:2.en: The lights flickered once, then went out completely. In the sudden dark, Tang grabbed a torch from under the counter without a word — she had clearly done this before. 'The *power* goes out every big sale weekend,' she said calmly. Outside, the street was dark too. We were completely alone.
power:2.cnHint: 促销周末____突然断了，阿糖镇定地从柜台下摸出手电筒，说这种事每次大促都会发生。
power:2.hook: Then someone knocked hard on the locked front door.
power:2.line: 'The *power* always cuts out on big sale nights — grab the torch.'

receive:2.en: A small envelope sat on the back counter when I arrived for my shift. Tang pointed at it with a grin. 'That is for you,' she said. I opened it slowly. Inside was a handwritten note from a regular customer — someone I had never even spoken to. I was surprised to *receive* such a kind message on only my third night.
receive:2.cnHint: 我在上班时____了一位常客写来的手写便条，感到十分意外。
receive:2.hook: But the note mentioned something hidden behind the rice-cooker shelf.
receive:2.line: 'I did not expect to *receive* anything so kind on my third night.'

encourage:2.en: The weekend sale turned the store into a small storm of shopping baskets and loud opinions. I fumbled with the price-gun and tagged a bag of chips at ten times the real cost. The Manager did not shout. Instead, she patted my shoulder and said the words I needed most right then. It meant a lot to have someone *encourage* me rather than laugh.
encourage:2.cnHint: 店长没有批评我贴错价格，而是____了我，让我感到温暖。
encourage:2.hook: Then she whispered that Lin had been watching from the door the whole time.
encourage:2.line: 'I always try to *encourage* new staff — mistakes are how you learn.'

travel:2.en: An old man came in just after two in the morning, rolling a large suitcase behind him. He bought a hot meat bun and ate it standing by the window, staring at the dark street. He told me he was about to *travel* alone across the country by train, the same route he and his wife had taken thirty years ago. His eyes were soft and far away.
travel:2.cnHint: 一位老人告诉我，他即将独自____，重走三十年前与妻子走过的路。
travel:2.hook: He left a small photograph on the counter and did not come back for it.
travel:2.line: 'At my age, every *travel* feels like the first one and the last one.'

strong:2.en: Tang brewed a fresh pot of coffee behind the counter and poured two cups without asking. She handed one to me and I took a sip — it hit the back of my throat like a friendly fist. The smell alone had kept me awake for an hour. 'You make *strong* coffee,' I told her, blinking. She just laughed and took a long, calm drink of her own cup.
strong:2.cnHint: 唐泡的咖啡味道____，浓得让我眨了眨眼睛。
strong:2.hook: She said she only made it that way after midnight, and there was a reason.
strong:2.line: 'I make it *strong* because the night is longer than people think.'

chance:2.en: Lin came in just before three, carrying a tray of sample snacks from the new store down the street. He set them on the counter and smiled at me like we were old friends. 'Try one,' he said. I did not know if I should — the Manager had never mentioned this kind of thing. Still, I thought it might be a *chance* to understand what we were really up against.
chance:2.cnHint: 林带来了对面新店的试吃零食，我觉得这是一个了解____的机会。
chance:2.hook: One of the samples had a note tucked underneath it, addressed to the Manager.
chance:2.line: 'Think of it as a *chance* to see what your customers might want next.'

solve:2.en: The card reader stopped working at the busiest moment of the sale — a line of six customers, all holding full baskets. I pressed every button I could find. Tang crouched behind the counter, traced the cable with two fingers, and found a loose plug. She pushed it in and looked up at me. 'Done,' she said. Watching her *solve* the problem in under a minute made me feel very new at this job.
solve:2.cnHint: 唐只用了不到一分钟就____了刷卡机的故障，让我佩服不已。
solve:2.hook: The last customer in line had been filming the whole thing on his phone.
solve:2.line: 'I have had to *solve* that same problem every weekend for two months.'

quite:2.en: By four in the morning the rush was over and the store felt *quite* different — still and warm, with the hum of the drink fridges filling the silence. I wiped down the counter and found myself enjoying it. One regular sat in the corner reading a thick book he had bought here every week for a month. I had never once seen him reach the last page.
quite:2.cnHint: 凌晨四点，店里____安静下来，只剩一位常客坐在角落看书。
quite:2.hook: Tonight, for the first time, I noticed he was reading it backwards.
quite:2.line: 'It is *quite* peaceful here after the crowds leave, is it not?'

technology:2.en: A teenager came in and stood in front of the new self-checkout screen the Manager had installed that afternoon. He tapped it, swiped it, tilted his head, and then walked to my counter instead. 'I prefer people,' he said, pushing his snacks toward me. I laughed. For all the *technology* the Manager loved to add, the regulars kept choosing the human lane.
technology:2.cnHint: 尽管店长引进了新____，这位常客还是更愿意找人工收银。
technology:2.hook: The teenager then asked if I knew who had left a voice message on the store's old phone.
technology:2.line: 'All this *technology* and people still queue for the human till — funny, right?'

education:2.en: A woman set a thick envelope on the counter and asked me to hold it until morning. 'It is for my son,' she said quietly. Inside, I could see the corner of a letter from a university. Whatever was written there would shape his whole *education* — and maybe the rest of his life.
education:2.cnHint: 一位母亲把一封信交给店员保管，那封信将决定她儿子未来的____。
education:2.hook: She never came back to pick it up.
education:2.line: 'A good *education* opens every door he will ever need.'

scientist:2.en: Just after two in the morning a man in a white coat hurried in, bought three energy drinks, and spread papers across the small window ledge. He muttered numbers to himself without stopping. Tang leaned over and whispered, 'That *scientist* comes every weekend. Nobody knows what he is working on.'
scientist:2.cnHint: 一位穿白大褂的____每个周末深夜都来店里，没有人知道他在研究什么。
scientist:2.hook: Last week he left one page behind, and it was covered in strange symbols.
scientist:2.line: 'I am a *scientist* — sleep can wait until the data is done.'

physical:2.en: The Manager taped a new notice to the door before his shift ended: 'Weekend Sale — all items checked for *physical* damage will be reduced by half.' He tapped the sign proudly. I stared at the shelf of dented cans he had quietly moved to the front row overnight.
physical:2.cnHint: 店长贴出促销告示，称有____损坏的商品将打五折，但我发现他把凹陷的罐头都悄悄摆到了最前排。
physical:2.hook: A customer picked up the biggest dented can and turned it over very slowly.
physical:2.line: 'Check for any *physical* damage before you put it on the shelf.'

quality:2.en: Lin walked in from the store across the street, picked up one of our rice balls, and studied the label for a long time. 'Not bad,' she said at last, sounding almost disappointed. I had learned by now that when Lin said 'not bad,' she really meant the *quality* was better than she had hoped.
quality:2.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林拿起一个饭团仔细研究，她说"还不错"——这其实意味着她认为____超出了预期。
quality:2.hook: She bought two before she walked back out without another word.
quality:2.line: 'I have to admit, the *quality* here is higher than I expected.'

habit:2.en: Every Saturday at midnight, an old man came in and bought exactly one small carton of warm milk and one sesame bun. He paid with coins he counted out slowly. Tang told me this was his *habit* for the past six years, ever since his wife passed away. Tonight he bought two buns.
habit:2.cnHint: 一位老人六年来每周六午夜都会来买同样的东西，这个____从未改变——直到今晚他多买了一个。
habit:2.hook: He looked at the second bun for a moment, then smiled at no one.
habit:2.line: 'Old *habit*, I suppose — I just cannot seem to stop coming here.'

sound:2.en: Around three in the morning I heard a soft *sound* near the back — a small tapping, steady and low. I found a folded note wedged behind the noodle shelf. It had a date, a time, and the single word 'remember' written in neat letters. No name, no other clue.
sound:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，店员在货架后面听到一阵____，随后发现了一张神秘的纸条。
sound:2.hook: The date on the note was tomorrow.
sound:2.line: 'Did you hear that *sound* coming from the back of the store just now?'

average:2.en: I rang up the weekend totals and showed them to the Manager. He nodded slowly. 'On *average*,' he said, tapping the screen, 'we sell forty cups of hot coffee per night. Tonight was sixty.' He paused. 'Someone is telling people about us.' He looked pleased, and a little suspicious.
average:2.cnHint: 店长查看周末营业数据，发现今晚的咖啡销量远超____水平，他高兴之余也有些起疑。
average:2.hook: The Manager asked me to check whether anyone had been posting about the store online.
average:2.line: 'On *average* we sell forty cups, so tonight is very unusual indeed.'

body:2.en: A delivery worker came in just before dawn, sat down on the small bench by the door, and did not move for ten minutes. 'Sorry,' he said at last, 'my *body* just stopped.' He smiled tiredly. I handed him a hot drink without being asked. He looked at it like it was the nicest thing that had happened all week.
body:2.cnHint: 一位送货员在快递了一夜后走进便利店，他说自己的____已经不听使唤了。
body:2.hook: When he finally stood to leave, he left a folded receipt on the bench with a short message on the back.
body:2.line: 'After twelve hours of riding, my *body* just does not want to move anymore.'

key:2.en: The Manager left a note taped to the register before my shift: 'The *key* to a busy weekend is knowing where everything is.' I spent ten minutes memorising the shelves. By midnight I could find any item blindfolded. Then a regular walked in looking for something we had never stocked.
key:2.cnHint: 店长留下纸条说，掌握____才能应对繁忙的周末促销。
key:2.hook: She asked for it by name, and her eyes said she had been searching for weeks.
key:2.line: 'The *key* to tonight is staying calm and keeping the shelves full.'

issue:2.en: Tang slid a thin magazine across the counter. 'New *issue* of the community newsletter,' she said. 'The Manager wants one copy kept here for regulars.' I set it beside the register. An old man came in at 2 a.m., picked it up, and turned straight to page seven without even glancing at the cover.
issue:2.cnHint: 阿糖带来了社区报纸的新____，放在收银台旁供常客取阅。
issue:2.hook: Whatever was on page seven made his hands go very still.
issue:2.line: 'This *issue* just arrived — leave a copy out where people can see it.'

against:2.en: I leaned *against* the cold glass door during the quiet hour before dawn, watching the empty street. Tang had warned me not to do that — 'You look like you are giving up,' she said. A woman in a yellow coat appeared from nowhere, pressed her face to the glass from outside, and stared straight at me.
against:2.cnHint: 我在黎明前的安静时刻____着玻璃门休息，结果被窗外的陌生人吓了一跳。
against:2.hook: She mouthed two words, then walked away before I could open the door.
against:2.line: 'Don't lean *against* the door — it makes the whole store look closed.'

matter:2.en: Lin came in from the store across the street, pretending to browse. 'No hard feelings,' Lin said, 'competition is just a *matter* of business.' I nodded and handed over a free coffee sample, the way the Manager had told me to. Lin looked surprised, then suspicious, then took a long sip and said nothing.
matter:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林假装闲逛来到店里，说竞争不过是生意上的____，随后接过了我递去的试饮咖啡。
matter:2.hook: Lin set the empty cup down and came back an hour later with a question.
matter:2.line: 'It's just a *matter* of time before your weekend sale beats ours.'

raise:2.en: During the Saturday rush the Manager pulled me aside. 'I am going to *raise* your hourly rate starting next week,' she said quietly. Before I could thank her, the line at the register grew six people deep and she was already counting change. I worked the rest of the shift in a kind of happy blur.
raise:2.cnHint: 周末促销高峰时，店长悄悄告诉我要____我的时薪，随后顾客队伍就排起来了。
raise:2.hook: One customer in that line had been listening, and he smiled like he knew something I did not.
raise:2.line: 'I plan to *raise* the hourly rate for everyone who works this weekend.'

option:2.en: The weekend sale flyer listed three bundle deals. A student stared at it for a long time. 'Only one *option* actually saves money,' I told her, pointing to the middle row. She thanked me, grabbed it, then hesitated at the door as if she had just remembered something important she had left behind.
option:2.cnHint: 周末促销传单上列了三种套餐，我告诉一位学生只有一种____真正划算。
option:2.hook: She came back in, but not for the item she had forgotten.
option:2.line: 'The best *option* for students is the middle bundle — it saves the most.'

society:2.en: Tang pinned a small poster near the snacks: 'Supported by the Night Owl *Society* — open all hours for people who need us.' I had never heard of it. 'Who are they?' I asked. Tang just smiled and said three of their members came in every single night at exactly 3 a.m., always together, always quiet.
society:2.cnHint: 阿糖贴出一张海报，说这家店受到一个名叫夜猫子____的组织支持。
society:2.hook: It was 2:58 a.m., and I heard footsteps outside already.
society:2.line: 'The Night Owl *Society* basically keeps this store alive on weeknights.'

whole:2.en: By Sunday close I had restocked the *whole* front wall of drinks twice over. The Manager looked around, nodded once, and said, 'Good.' Tang gave me a thumbs-up. Then I found a folded note tucked under the register mat — no name, just six words in small, careful letters.
whole:2.cnHint: 到了周日打烊时，我已经把整____面饮料货架补货了两次，收银台下还藏着一张纸条。
whole:2.hook: The six words told me the store had a secret I had not been shown.
whole:2.line: 'You restocked the *whole* front wall? That usually takes two people.'

animal:2.en: During the weekend sale, a small cardboard box sat near the magazine rack. I almost walked past it, but a soft sound made me stop. Inside, wrapped in an old scarf, was a tiny *animal* — a kitten, eyes still closed. A folded note on top read: 'Please keep her warm.'
animal:2.cnHint: 收银台旁的纸箱里，有人留下了一只小____，还附了一张纸条。
animal:2.hook: The note had the Manager's handwriting on the back.
animal:2.line: 'An *animal* this small needs warm milk, not cold air.'

goal:2.en: Tang had taped a hand-written list to the staff fridge. At the top, in big letters: 'Weekend Sale *Goal* — 500 drinks sold by Sunday night.' Below it, a row of small boxes to tick. By Saturday noon, only three boxes were filled. Tang stared at the list and sighed loudly.
goal:2.cnHint: 唐在冰箱上贴了一张清单，写着本次大促的销售____，但进度让人叹气。
goal:2.hook: Then Lin walked in, marker in hand, and crossed out '500'.
goal:2.line: 'Our *goal* is 500 — we are not closing early, understand?'

adult:2.en: A boy, maybe ten years old, placed a bottle of energy drink on the counter with great seriousness. I shook my head and pointed to the small sign above the shelf. He read it slowly, then looked up. 'But I am nearly an *adult*,' he said. I smiled and handed him a juice instead.
adult:2.cnHint: 一个小男孩想买功能饮料，却被告知那是____才能买的东西。
adult:2.hook: He left the juice untouched and came back an hour later with someone taller.
adult:2.line: 'I am practically an *adult* — just check how tall I am!'

poor:2.en: The heating fan in the back room stopped working at midnight. Tang wrapped himself in an unsold scarf from the display stand and sat behind the counter looking miserable. 'Look at this *poor* clerk,' said Lin, walking in with two hot cups from the machine, 'freezing behind his own shelf.'
poor:2.cnHint: 深夜暖风机坏了，唐冷得可____，林进来时忍不住调侃他。
poor:2.hook: Lin set one cup down — then picked it back up with a grin.
poor:2.line: '*Poor* Tang, shall I charge you for this hot cup?'

price:2.en: A regular customer held up a bottle of green tea and pointed at the shelf label. 'The *price* changed again,' she said, not angry, just tired. I checked the system. She was right — someone had updated the tags but forgotten this one row. I fixed it and gave her the lower amount.
price:2.cnHint: 一位常客发现货架上的____没有更新，多收了钱。
price:2.hook: The old label, when I turned it over, had the Manager's initials on it.
price:2.line: 'The *price* on the shelf and the price at the till should match, yes?'

type:2.en: Lin slid a stack of new membership cards across the counter. 'There is a new *type* this month — gold, silver, and basic. Learn the difference before the morning rush.' I studied the three cards. They looked almost identical. I turned them over. The only difference was a tiny number in the corner.
type:2.cnHint: 林拿来新版会员卡，向我介绍有三种不同的____，但它们看起来几乎一样。
type:2.hook: Customer number one walked in forty seconds later, card already in hand.
type:2.line: 'This *type* of card gets an extra five percent off — do not forget.'

sense:2.en: At 3 a.m. the store was empty and very quiet. I straightened a row of canned soup just to have something to do. Then a strange *sense* of being watched came over me. I turned around slowly. The Manager was standing at the door in his coat, saying nothing, just nodding once.
sense:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，我突然有一种被注视的____，转身一看，店长就站在门口。
sense:2.hook: He left without a word, but a folded paper sat on the mat.
sense:2.line: 'You have good *sense* — the soup row needed fixing half an hour ago.'

rate:2.en: Tang was on the phone, pacing between the drinks fridge and the door. 'At this *rate*,' he said loudly, 'we will still be here at noon counting leftover stock.' The weekend promotion was ending in two hours. Two full pallets of boxed juice sat untouched near the window. Tang ended the call and looked at me.
rate:2.cnHint: 唐看着卖剩的库存，担心按这个____下去，大促结束前根本卖不完。
rate:2.hook: He handed me a marker and pointed at the window facing the street.
rate:2.line: 'At this *rate* we will be drinking boxed juice for the next two weeks.'

nearly:2.en: During the weekend sale, the back storeroom became a maze of boxes. I was sent to find extra bags but got lost among the towers of stock. I *nearly* knocked over a whole shelf of instant noodles before Tang appeared from behind a box, torch in hand, grinning like he owned the place.
nearly:2.cnHint: 我在仓库找备用袋子时，____撞倒了一排货架。
nearly:2.hook: Tang's torch lit something on the shelf that should not have been there.
nearly:2.line: 'You *nearly* took out six months of noodle stock, new kid.'

wrong:2.en: A note was taped to the staff fridge during the sale rush. It listed names and break times, but my name was on the *wrong* shift — midnight instead of ten. I stared at it, bag still on my shoulder. Tang leaned over, read it, and quietly peeled the note off without a word.
wrong:2.cnHint: 休息时间表上我的名字被安排在了____的班次。
wrong:2.hook: Tang folded the note and slipped it into his own pocket.
wrong:2.line: 'Your time slot is *wrong* — someone changed it after I posted it.'

variety:2.en: The weekend sale brought a *variety* of customers I had never seen on quiet weeknights: families with big trolleys, students grabbing energy drinks, an elderly man inspecting every single rice ball. The Manager watched from behind the counter, nodding slowly, as if each new face confirmed something he had long suspected.
variety:2.cnHint: 周末促销吸引了各种____的顾客，店长若有所思地观察着。
variety:2.hook: The elderly man finally chose nothing and asked for the Manager by name.
variety:2.line: 'A *variety* of people show up this weekend — watch them carefully.'

clear:2.en: A handwritten sign had fallen from the freezer door and landed behind the ice-cream tubs. I found it while restocking. The words were still *clear*: 'Reserved — do not sell. — Lin.' Below the sign sat a single can of peach tea, alone in the corner, waiting like a small secret.
clear:2.cnHint: 冰柜角落里有一张字迹____的手写纸条，是隔壁咖啡店的林留下的。
clear:2.hook: The date written under Lin's name was tomorrow.
clear:2.line: 'Is it *clear* whose drink that is? Because it has been there a week.'

gain:2.en: After the sale rush, Tang sat on the back step counting the loyalty-stamp cards customers had forgotten at the counter. 'Each stamp is a small *gain*,' he said, more to himself than to me, lining them up like a short fence. There were eleven. He looked at them the way you look at a puzzle with a missing piece.
gain:2.cnHint: 阿糖数着顾客遗落的积分卡，说每张卡都是一种小小的____。
gain:2.hook: One card had a name on the back written in red ink.
gain:2.line: 'Every forgotten card is a *gain* for whoever claims it first.'

maybe:2.en: A small box arrived in the morning delivery with no store label, only a sticky note that read 'for the clerk on nights.' I turned it over twice. Tang shrugged. '*Maybe* it is from a regular,' he said, going back to his mop. The Manager looked up from his clipboard, said nothing, and went back to his numbers.
maybe:2.cnHint: 一个没有标签的包裹出现在早班货物里，阿糖说____是常客送的。
maybe:2.hook: Inside the box was a single key with no lock in sight.
maybe:2.line: '*Maybe* someone wanted you to find it before the Manager did.'

huge:2.en: The promotion display near the entrance had grown overnight. By Saturday morning it was a *huge* tower of snack boxes, almost touching the ceiling light. A small paper flag on top read 'SALE' in red. Tang said he had not built it. I said I had not either. We both looked at the Manager.
huge:2.cnHint: 促销堆头变成了一座____的零食塔，没人知道是谁搭的。
huge:2.hook: The Manager smiled and walked away before either of us could ask.
huge:2.line: 'That *huge* display went up between two and four — I checked the log.'

diet:2.en: A regular customer came in just before sunrise, picked up her usual yoghurt, then stood for a long time in front of the new snack wall. 'I am meant to be on a *diet*,' she said to no one. She put the yoghurt back, picked up a small bag of nuts instead, and left looking genuinely surprised at herself.
diet:2.cnHint: 一位常客说自己在____，最后却出乎意料地换了一样东西买走。
diet:2.hook: She paused at the door and glanced back at the yoghurt shelf.
diet:2.line: 'My *diet* plan says nuts are fine — probably.'

within:2.en: A folded note sat under the milk bottles near the back cooler. It read: 'Please restock the top shelf *within* one hour — a big order is coming.' No name, no time stamp. I looked around the empty store. Someone had been here and left before I even noticed the door.
within:2.cnHint: 我在冷藏柜旁发现一张纸条，要求在____一小时内补货。
within:2.hook: But the top shelf had already been restocked — by someone else.
within:2.line: 'Get it done *within* the hour, or the Manager will notice,' the note said.

either:2.en: Two identical red envelopes sat on the counter when I arrived for my shift. One had my name on it, one had Tang's. I asked Tang which one to open first. Tang shrugged: 'I haven't opened *either* of mine yet.' There were two envelopes for Tang. We stared at each other in silence.
either:2.cnHint: 柜台上放着两个红包，我和阿糖____都还没拆开自己的那份。
either:2.hook: The third envelope, addressed to no one, was tucked behind the register.
either:2.line: 'I haven't touched *either* one — I was waiting for you,' Tang said quietly.

various:2.en: Behind the storage room door I found a corkboard covered in papers. The Manager had pinned up *various* notes about our regulars — preferred snacks, usual visit times, even small personal details. 'Old Mr. Chen: bad knees, needs low shelf.' I felt I had just found a secret map of the whole neighbourhood.
various:2.cnHint: 储藏室里有一块软木板，上面贴满了店长关于各位常客的____种各样的备注。
various:2.hook: One note had a name I had never heard — and a red question mark beside it.
various:2.line: 'The Manager keeps *various* notes on everyone who comes in,' Tang whispered.

main:2.en: The *main* supply box for the weekend sale had arrived, but it was locked. A small card taped to the lid said the key was hidden somewhere in the store. I spent twenty minutes searching. Tang watched me from behind a magazine, clearly trying not to laugh.
main:2.cnHint: 周末大促的____主要货箱到了，却是锁着的，钥匙藏在店里某处。
main:2.hook: Tang knew exactly where the key was — and said nothing.
main:2.line: 'The *main* box is always locked on delivery day,' Tang said, finally smiling.

employee:2.en: Tucked inside the new staff handbook on the back shelf was an old photo. It showed three young people in store uniforms standing outside this very corner. On the back someone had written: 'First day — the best team.' I turned it over. One face looked exactly like the Manager, twenty years younger. Every *employee* here carries a story.
employee:2.cnHint: 员工手册里夹着一张旧照片，原来每一位____都有自己的故事。
employee:2.hook: The third person in the photo was someone I had not yet met.
employee:2.line: 'Every *employee* finds that photo eventually,' Tang said, not looking up.

class:2.en: A student left her notebook on the counter and rushed out. I flipped it open to find the owner's name. The page read: '*Class* 3, Building B — if lost, please call—' followed by a number that had been crossed out and rewritten three times. She had been changing her number a lot lately. I hoped she was okay.
class:2.cnHint: 一个学生落下了笔记本，封面写着____3班的信息，联系电话却改了好几次。
class:2.hook: She came back an hour later, eyes red, and asked if anyone had called.
class:2.line: '*Class* 3 students always come in after their late lab,' Tang said softly.

behavior:2.en: The Manager left a short handwritten memo on the register. It said: 'Please observe and note any unusual *behavior* near the east window after 2 a.m. — no action needed, just record it.' I read it twice. The east window faced the quiet alley where nothing ever happened. Or so I had thought.
behavior:2.cnHint: 店长留下一张便条，要求记录东侧窗边出现的任何异常____行为。
behavior:2.hook: At 2:07 a.m., a shadow paused at the east window for a full minute.
behavior:2.line: 'His *behavior* changes every time it rains,' Tang said, glancing at the window.

disease:2.en: A regular named Old Wu always bought the same herbal drink and nothing else. Tonight he left a folded flyer on the counter. It was about a community talk on a common winter *disease* — the kind that spreads fast in cold, dry air. He had circled the date and written: 'Bring your young staff.' He was looking out for us.
disease:2.cnHint: 常客老吴留下了一张关于冬季常见____疾病讲座的传单，还特意圈出了日期。
disease:2.hook: The date circled was tomorrow night — and Old Wu had already saved us seats.
disease:2.line: 'This *disease* spreads fast once the heating comes on,' Old Wu had written at the top.

mind:2.en: Tang slid a folded note across the counter. 'The Manager left this for you,' she said, then disappeared into the back room. I opened it: a hand-drawn map of every shelf, with little arrows and labels in neat handwriting. Someone had put real *mind* into it — every corner of the store accounted for, even the tricky spot behind the rice cooker display. I felt, for the first time, genuinely welcome.
mind:2.cnHint: 店长留下了一张手绘地图，让新店员感受到了____的用心。
mind:2.hook: But one shelf on the map had a question mark where a price should be.
mind:2.line: 'Whoever drew this put serious *mind* into it — look at all these little notes.'

rise:2.en: I noticed it around 2 a.m.: a slow, steady *rise* in the number of customers. First one student with a bag of chips, then three more, then a whole group carrying notebooks. Tang leaned over and whispered, 'Weekend exam season. It happens every time.' She pulled extra cup-noodle stock from the back without being asked. The store hummed quietly to life.
rise:2.cnHint: 深夜两点，便利店的客流开始____，原来是考试季来了。
rise:2.hook: One student kept glancing at the door as if waiting for someone who was very late.
rise:2.line: 'Every exam weekend we see a *rise* in night customers — stock the noodles now.'

prove:2.en: A handwritten sign taped to the drinks fridge read: 'Cold drinks — guaranteed coldest on the street.' Tang said Lin from the corner shop had put up the same sign last week. 'So the Manager wrote ours first thing this morning,' she added, smiling. It was a small thing, but it seemed important to *prove* the store still led the street, even in tiny details.
prove:2.cnHint: 店长贴出告示，想____自家便利店在街上仍是最好的。
prove:2.hook: Lin walked past the window at that exact moment and stared at the sign for a long time.
prove:2.line: 'We need to *prove* we are still the best shop on this corner — every detail counts.'

associate:2.en: I found an old photo tucked behind the counter — two young people standing in front of what looked like an earlier version of this very store. Tang glanced at it and said quietly, 'That is the Manager and an old *associate*. They opened this place together years ago.' She did not say more. I set the photo gently back where I had found it, feeling I had touched something private.
associate:2.cnHint: 一张旧照片揭示了店长曾经有一位____，两人共同开创了这家小店。
associate:2.hook: The second person in the photo had their name tag turned so you could not read it.
associate:2.line: 'That person was the Manager's *associate* — they built this store together from nothing.'

message:2.en: At half past midnight, the store phone rang — an odd thing, since almost no one used it. I picked up. Silence, then a careful voice: 'Please give the Manager a *message* — the old supplier is back in town.' I wrote it on a sticky note and pressed it to the register. Tang saw it, raised an eyebrow, and said nothing at all, which somehow felt louder than any reply.
message:2.cnHint: 一个神秘的电话留下了一条____，阿糖的反应却让人觉得事情不简单。
message:2.hook: The Manager arrived an hour early the next morning and went straight for the sticky note.
message:2.line: 'Can you give the Manager a *message*? Tell him the old supplier called tonight.'

development:2.en: I asked Tang why the store stayed open all night when the street was so quiet after 1 a.m. She pointed to a printed notice near the door: a new residential block was under construction two streets over. 'That *development* will bring hundreds of new neighbors by spring,' she said. 'The Manager wants them to already think of us as their store before they even move in.' Smart, I thought.
development:2.cnHint: 附近的楼盘____让店长提前布局，想赢得未来新邻居的信任。
development:2.hook: The notice listed a completion date — and it was only six weeks away.
development:2.line: 'That housing *development* nearby will change everything for this little store by spring.'

later:2.en: I shelved a box of green-tea sweets and thought nothing of it. An hour *later*, a woman in a paint-stained coat came in, walked directly to that shelf, picked up one packet, and held it to her chest like it was something rare. She paid without a word and left just as quietly. Tang watched her go and said, 'She comes every Saturday. Same item. Every time.' I wanted to know why.
later:2.cnHint: 一位神秘女顾客每周六都会来买同一样东西，这让新店员____充满好奇。
later:2.hook: The woman paused just outside the door, looked back once, then walked into the dark.
later:2.line: 'An hour *later* she always comes back — same shelf, same item, no matter what.'

maintain:2.en: Tang handed me a small printed checklist before my first solo hour at the register. 'The Manager says it is the only way to *maintain* the good feeling of the store,' she explained. Every box covered something small: wipe the counter, face the products outward, check the music volume. I followed each step carefully. By 3 a.m. the store felt almost as neat as when I had arrived, which felt like a quiet victory.
maintain:2.cnHint: 一份细心的清单帮助新店员____便利店整洁温馨的氛围。
maintain:2.hook: The last item on the checklist was crossed out in red ink, with no explanation given.
maintain:2.line: 'Follow this list every hour to *maintain* the warm feeling customers expect from us.'

worker:2.en: A note was taped to the back-room door when I arrived for my shift. It read: 'The *worker* who stacked the east shelf left early — please recheck the dates.' I found three expired yoghurts hiding behind the new ones. The Manager had known all along, I think.
worker:2.cnHint: 我在仓库门上发现一张便条，提醒我检查东边货架上的____摆放是否有问题。
worker:2.hook: But the note was signed with a name I did not recognise.
worker:2.line: 'The *worker* who was here last night forgot to rotate the stock again.'

control:2.en: The weekend sale turned the store into gentle chaos. Tang handled the line at the register while I tried to *control* the crowd around the snack display — people kept reaching past each other and knocking things over. I restacked the same shelf four times. Tang just laughed each time.
control:2.cnHint: 周末促销时店里乱作一团，我努力____着零食区的秩序，但总是徒劳。
control:2.hook: Then one quiet customer in the corner had not moved for twenty minutes.
control:2.line: 'I can *control* the register side — you just keep that snack shelf tidy.'

product:2.en: I found a small handwritten card tucked under a shelf: 'This *product* changed my life — please keep it in stock.' It was attached to a plain tin of ginger candy on the bottom row. I had walked past it a hundred times without noticing. I ordered three extra boxes that night.
product:2.cnHint: 我在货架下发现一张小卡片，有人留言说某款____改变了他们的生活。
product:2.hook: I still wonder who left that card, and whether they ever came back.
product:2.line: 'Every *product* on that bottom shelf sells better than it looks — trust me.'

practice:2.en: Lin appeared just before midnight, notepad in hand, quietly checking our shelf labels against their own. 'Standard *practice*,' Lin said, not unkindly, when I raised an eyebrow. I said nothing. But after Lin left I checked every label twice, just to be sure.
practice:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜来店里对比货架标签，说这是他们的常规____。
practice:2.hook: What Lin wrote in that notepad, I still have not figured out.
practice:2.line: 'It is just normal *practice* — we check every store on the street on weekends.'

environment:2.en: The Manager had strung a second set of warm lights above the drink fridge for the weekend sale, and the whole store felt different — softer, almost festive. 'A better *environment* sells more,' she said, handing me the remote for the lights. I quietly agreed. It was working on me too.
environment:2.cnHint: 店长为大促特别布置了灯光，说良好的____能提升销量。
environment:2.hook: She handed me the remote, then added one thing I was not expecting.
environment:2.line: 'A warm *environment* makes people stay a little longer — and spend a little more.'

system:2.en: During the rush I knocked the paper receipt roll behind the counter and the whole register *system* jammed. Tang talked me through the reset, step by step, calm as anything. Thirty seconds later it was fine. I asked how Tang knew that. Tang just shrugged: 'I read the manual.'
system:2.cnHint: 我不小心弄坏了收银____，阿糖淡定地一步步教我重置。
system:2.hook: Tang mentioned the manual so casually — but no manual was anywhere in sight.
system:2.line: 'The whole *system* resets if you hold the two side buttons at the same time.'

natural:2.en: A girl came in looking embarrassed, holding a crumpled list. She asked quietly if we had a certain herbal tea. 'It is *natural*, no additives,' she explained, as if she needed to justify herself. We had it. She looked so relieved that I nearly smiled. She bought two boxes.
natural:2.cnHint: 一位女生羞怯地询问我们是否有某款____的花草茶，神情如释重负。
natural:2.hook: She paused at the door and looked back at one other shelf for a long moment.
natural:2.line: 'I only drink things that are *natural* — no colors, no extra stuff added.'

free:2.en: A handwritten sign had appeared on the counter: 'One small candy *free* with every purchase over fifteen yuan — weekend only.' Nobody told me about it. Customers kept pointing at the sign with hopeful looks. I honoured it all night. The Manager never mentioned it the next morning.
free:2.cnHint: 柜台上出现了一张手写的告示，说消费满额可获赠____糖果，但没人提前告诉我。
free:2.hook: The sign was gone by sunrise, as if it had never been there.
free:2.line: 'Just grab one *free* candy from the jar — you are over fifteen yuan, so it is fine.'

action:2.en: The Manager taped a bright sign to the door this morning: WEEKEND SALE. By midnight the shelf with the rice crackers was almost empty. I stood behind the counter watching customers grab and go. Every *action* in the store felt faster than usual, like everyone had somewhere urgent to be. Then one old man just stood still, reading the back of a snack bag for a very long time.
action:2.cnHint: 周末大促期间，店里每个人的____都比平时快，但有位老人却站着不动，仔细看着零食包装的背面。
action:2.hook: He turned the bag over and over, and his hands would not stop shaking.
action:2.line: 'Every *action* tonight has been fast — except yours, sir.'

program:2.en: Tang pulled out a crumpled paper from under the counter. It was the Manager's handwritten *program* for the weekend sale: restock at six, run the discount scanner at eight, count the drawer at midnight. Tang circled the midnight step and pointed at me with a grin. So the cash-counting job was mine. Fine. But the paper had a fourth item someone had crossed out in red ink.
program:2.cnHint: 唐从柜台下面找出店长手写的周末促销____，上面有一条被红笔划掉了。
program:2.hook: Whatever that crossed-out item said, Tang refused to tell me.
program:2.line: 'The *program* says you count the drawer at midnight — good luck.'

situation:2.en: Around two in the morning a woman rushed in, phone pressed to her ear, whispering fast. She looked around the store with wide eyes. I asked if she needed help. She said, 'I just need a moment to think.' I have seen busy people and tired people, but her *situation* felt different — like she was solving something much bigger than a late-night snack run. She bought nothing. She just left a folded note on the counter.
situation:2.cnHint: 凌晨两点，一位女士冲进店里，她的____让我觉得她不只是来买东西的，她走时留下了一张折叠的纸条。
situation:2.hook: The note had only two words and a phone number I did not recognise.
situation:2.line: 'My *situation* is complicated — please just let me stand here a minute.'

order:2.en: The delivery boxes arrived early and in no sensible *order*: chips on top of bread, cold drinks beside the hot-food shelf, three boxes marked FRAGILE stacked at the very bottom. I spent an hour sorting everything before the morning rush. When the Manager checked at six, she nodded once and said nothing. That nod felt like a gold medal. Then she pointed at one box I had missed behind the mop bucket.
order:2.cnHint: 送货箱子到了，但____全乱了，我花了一个小时整理，店长点了点头，但又指向了我漏掉的一个箱子。
order:2.hook: Inside that last box was something the invoice did not list.
order:2.line: 'Please put these in *order* before the morning crowd arrives.'

event:2.en: Lin from the store across the street appeared just after midnight, holding a flyer. Their shop was running a big *event* on Sunday — free tea samples, a lucky draw, the works. Lin smiled and slid the flyer across my counter without a word. I smiled back and slid it into the recycling. We both understood. When Lin left, I noticed they had actually bought a bottle of water. Even rivals get thirsty.
event:2.cnHint: 午夜后，竞争对手林走进来，悄悄放下了他们店周日活动的传单，介绍了一场特别的____，然后买了瓶水离开。
event:2.hook: Lin paused at the door, glanced back once, then smiled a little too long.
event:2.line: 'Our *event* Sunday will be very popular — just letting you know.'

account:2.en: A regular I had not seen before handed me a store membership card that would not scan. I tried three times. He gave a long *account* of how he had used it just last week, how the Manager herself had set it up, how it had worked perfectly until tonight. His story was detailed and patient. I called the Manager. She had never seen the card before. The man nodded slowly, as if he had expected this answer.
account:2.cnHint: 一位顾客的会员卡扫不出来，他详细____了卡的使用历史，但店长说从没见过这张卡。
account:2.hook: He put the card back in his wallet next to six others that looked exactly the same.
account:2.line: 'Let me give you a full *account* of how I got this card.'

deal:2.en: Tang had made a quiet *deal* with the supplier: buy two boxes of green-tea candy, get one box of fruit candy free. It was a good arrangement, and Tang was proud of it. I found out because all three boxes were hidden behind the instant noodles with a sticky note that said DO NOT SELL — TANG. The Manager found them at the same time I did. They looked at each other for a long, quiet second.
deal:2.cnHint: 唐私下和供应商做了个____，把换来的糖果藏在泡面后面，结果被店长和我同时发现了。
deal:2.hook: Tang's smile did not waver, but both hands gripped the shelf very tight.
deal:2.line: 'It was a fair *deal* — the supplier agreed, I promise.'

degree:2.en: The old heater behind the counter had one dial with numbers worn off. Tang said to turn it to 'medium,' but without marks that meant nothing. By three in the morning the store had reached a *degree* of warmth that made every customer slow down and linger, like they had all walked into a cosy living room by accident. Even the cat from the alley outside pressed its nose to the glass door. Then the power flickered once.
degree:2.cnHint: 老暖气的刻度盘数字都磨掉了，夜里店里暖到了某种____，让每个顾客都不想走，连巷子里的猫都趴到玻璃门上了。
degree:2.hook: When the lights came back, the cat was somehow inside the store.
degree:2.line: 'The *degree* of warmth in here tonight is really something special.'

traditional:2.en: The Manager taped a hand-written sign above the rice-ball shelf before my shift started. 'We do things the *traditional* way here,' he said, meaning he wrote every price by hand instead of printing labels. The sign was a little crooked, but the customers smiled every time they read it.
traditional:2.cnHint: 店长坚持用手写价签，因为他觉得这才是____的做法。
traditional:2.hook: But one sign at the back of the shelf was not his handwriting.
traditional:2.line: 'We do things the *traditional* way here — handwritten, personal, honest.'

expert:2.en: A quiet woman came in just after two in the morning and stood in front of the instant-noodle wall for a long time. She picked up each cup, read the back, and put it down again. Tang leaned over to me and whispered that she was a food *expert* who tested products for a living. She bought nothing and left a small note on the counter instead.
expert:2.cnHint: 一位深夜光顾的女顾客是食品____，她仔细检查了每一款泡面。
expert:2.hook: The note had a score written on it — and our store got a seven out of ten.
expert:2.line: 'As a food *expert*, I can tell you — three of these noodles are worth buying.'

member:2.en: An old man shuffled in and slid a worn card across the counter. It was a loyalty card from before I started working here — nearly full of stamps. 'I am the oldest *member* of this store,' he said proudly, tapping the card twice. I did not know what prize he expected, but his smile suggested he had already decided.
member:2.cnHint: 一位老爷爷拿出快集满的会员卡，自豪地说自己是本店最老的____。
member:2.hook: The back of the card had a phone number written in red ink — the Manager's personal number.
member:2.line: 'I am the oldest *member* of this store, young one — I was here on opening night.'

heart:2.en: Around three in the morning the street outside went completely silent. Tang set two warm canned drinks on the counter without a word and said, 'The *heart* of a night shift is the quiet hour — you either love it or it breaks you.' I wrapped both hands around the can and decided, right then, that I loved it.
heart:2.cnHint: 阿糖说深夜值班的____就是这段寂静时光，让我第一次感受到了夜班的魅力。
heart:2.hook: Then footsteps — quick, uneven — stopped just outside the glass door.
heart:2.line: 'The *heart* of night shift is this hour — hold onto it.'
